jahmyr gibbs.verdict: Elite dual-threat with two straight 360+ seasons and rising receiving role; RB1 overall
jahmyr gibbs.report: Gibbs posted 21.6 PPG on 94 targets/243 carries in 2025, backing up 2024's 21.3 PPG, so he's a proven three-down back with 84 first downs and a 1.04 rec EPA/g. Ceiling is the overall RB1 if his target share climbs past 16%; the floor stays high because Detroit's offense funnels him volume even alongside Pacheco. The only drag is a committee that keeps his carries capped and a slightly negative rush EPA. Playoff slate (@MIN, NYG, @CHI) is neutral-to-good.

bijan robinson.verdict: True workhorse with 287 carries + 103 targets and elite 1.56 rec EPA/g; safest RB floor
bijan robinson.report: Bijan combined 287 carries and 103 targets in 2025 for 21.8 PPG with a low 10.0 stdev, the picture of a bell-cow whose receiving role (19.8% target share, 0.31 WOPR) is now genuinely elite. Ceiling is the overall RB1 given Atlanta's lean on him and 97 first downs. Floor is elite thanks to that volume and low week-to-week variance. Brian Robinson's arrival is only a minor goal-line concern; playoff schedule (@WSH, TB, NO) is favorable.

christian mccaffrey.verdict: League-winning 2025 (417 pts) but age 30 and 2024 injury wipeout cap the price
christian mccaffrey.report: When healthy in 2025 CMC was untouchable: 417 points, 24.5 PPG, 129 targets, a 23.4% target share and absurd 2.30 rec EPA/g. But 2024's 2.8 PPG over an injury-shattered season is the reason he falls to ADP 6, and he's now a nine-year vet. Ceiling is the outright RB1 and a title on your roster; floor is a lost year if the soft-tissue issues recur. San Francisco has no threat behind him, but the injury tax is real; playoffs (@LAC, @KC, PHI) are tough.

jonathan taylor.verdict: Rushing workhorse with 323 carries and league-best rush EPA; limited pass game caps ceiling
jonathan taylor.report: Taylor rebounded to 21.3 PPG in 2025 on a massive 323 carries and a positive 1.10 rush EPA/g, a huge leap from 2024's 14.4 PPG. The floor is strong as Indy's clear early-down and goal-line hammer with 99 first downs and no real competition behind (Giddens #2). Ceiling is limited by an 11% target share and 0.16 WOPR — he's TD- and volume-dependent rather than a PPR receiving asset. Higher weekly variance (12.1 stdev) than the top tier; playoffs (@TEN, CIN, @CLE) are fine.

de'von achane.verdict: Explosive receiving back with 85 targets two years running; injury tag and MIA offense are risks
de'von achane.report: Achane has back-to-back strong seasons (19.0 then 17.6 PPG) fueled by a heavy receiving role — 85 targets and an 18.8% share in 2025 with a 0.29 WOPR. Ceiling is a top-five finish given his big-play juice (0.88 rush EPA/g). Floor concerns are the negative rec EPA, a shaky Miami passing environment, and the current Questionable injury tag. Wright and Gordon exist but Achane owns the clear lead role; playoff finish vs BUF in Week 17 is tough.

jeremiyah love.verdict: Hyped rookie handed the ARI backfield lead; boom projection but zero NFL data
jeremiyah love.report: Love enters as Arizona's RB1 with a 279-point projection and ADP 17, a bet on talent and opportunity with no pro track record. Ceiling is a rookie-of-the-year type breakout if he seizes three-down work over Allgeier and a fading James Conner. Floor is genuinely murky — rookie backs bust often and the depth chart lists veterans who could siphon touches early. The Week 15-17 slate (NYJ, @NO, LV) is soft, a real plus for playoff-week production.

james cook iii.verdict: Efficient volume runner in a great offense; 309 carries but thin pass usage limits PPR upside
james cook iii.report: Cook jumped to 17.8 PPG in 2025 on a career-high 309 carries, backing up 2024's 15.7 PPG in Buffalo's elite scoring offense. Ceiling comes from TD volume in a top offense; floor is steadied by workload. The catch is only ~35 targets a year, so his PPR ceiling is TD-dependent rather than reception-driven. Buffalo's offense keeps his floor firm; playoff schedule (CHI, @DEN, @MIA) is a mixed bag.

ashton jeanty.verdict: High-volume sophomore but brutal -3.83 rush EPA/g behind a bad LV line is a warning
ashton jeanty.report: Jeanty logged 266 carries and 73 targets as a rookie for 14.4 PPG, but the advanced numbers are ugly — a -3.83 rush EPA/g and -5.8% air-yards share point to a poor offensive environment. Ceiling is a big second-year leap with improved efficiency and receiving usage (55 catches already). Floor is real given the Raiders' line and offense drag his production down. He owns the backfield outright, and the playoff slate (DEN, TEN, @ARI) is neutral.

omarion hampton.verdict: Ascending LAC lead back but only 9 games in 2025; usage volatility is the risk
omarion hampton.report: Hampton flashed a receiving role (32 catches, 11.8% target share) but managed just 136 points across a nine-game 2025 season, so the sample is thin. Ceiling is a full three-down workhorse in the Chargers offense if he stays healthy and Keaton Mitchell doesn't cut in. Floor is a timeshare or another injury-shortened campaign. The workload projection (279) is a bet on volume; playoff schedule (SF, @MIA, KC) is difficult.

saquon barkley.verdict: Big 2024 (355) collapsed to 13.7 PPG in 2025 with -1.51 rush EPA; boom-bust at ADP 17
saquon barkley.report: Barkley cratered from a monster 2024 (20.9 PPG, 345 carries) to just 13.7 PPG in 2025 with a troubling -1.51 rush EPA/g and shrinking receiving role (12% target share). Ceiling is a bounce-back toward 300+ if Philadelphia's line and script revert. Floor is scary given the age-eight-year mileage and the added competition of Tank Bigsby. The wide gap between his two seasons makes him one of the higher-variance backs here; playoff finish (SEA, HOU, @SF) is average.

derrick henry.verdict: Age-32 volume back sliding from 19.8 to 16.4 PPG; elite TD equity but no pass-game floor
derrick henry.report: Henry remained productive at 16.4 PPG on 307 carries in 2025 but declined from 2024's 19.8 with a still-positive 0.54 rush EPA/g. Ceiling relies on goal-line TD equity in Baltimore's strong offense (83 first downs). Floor is thin because he catches almost nothing (4.9% target share, 0.07 WOPR) — one non-scoring week tanks him. Age 10-year mileage is the elephant in the room; playoffs (@PIT, CLE, @CIN) include tough divisional matchups.

josh jacobs.verdict: Steady TD-reliant back but 2025 dipped to 13.9 PPG with -0.99 rush EPA; MarShawn Lloyd looms
josh jacobs.report: Jacobs slid from 17.2 PPG in 2024 to 13.9 in 2025 with a negative rush EPA/g despite a healthy TD floor in Green Bay's offense. Ceiling is a return to RB1 numbers if he holds 300 touches. Floor is capped by a low 10.2% target share and creeping backfield competition from MarShawn Lloyd. He remains the clear early-down and goal-line back; playoff schedule (MIA, @CHI, HOU) is reasonable.

chase brown.verdict: Three-down role with 88 targets and 69 catches; PPR-friendly but efficiency and CIN line are concerns
chase brown.report: Brown offers a genuine PPR profile — 69 catches, 88 targets and a 0.22 WOPR in 2025 with 16.6 PPG and a very stable 7.1 stdev. Ceiling is a low-end RB1 if Cincinnati's high-powered passing game keeps feeding him targets. Floor is supported by that receiving volume, though the -0.61 rec and -0.25 rush EPA point to shaky efficiency. Perine is only a change-of-pace; playoff slate (@CAR, @IND, BAL) is favorable early.

breece hall.verdict: Talented but usage and efficiency slipped again; Braelon Allen committee caps the upside
breece hall.report: Hall fell to 12.2 PPG in 2025 with a -1.39 rush EPA/g and a shrinking receiving role (36 catches vs 57 in 2024). Ceiling is a bounce-back if the Jets clear the backfield and his pass-game usage returns. Floor is a frustrating timeshare with Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis eating goal-line and early-down work. The trend line is heading the wrong way; playoff schedule (@ARI, NE, MIN) is a mixed bag.

kenneth walker iii.verdict: New KC role could unlock volume but 2025 was low-efficiency; timeshare risk in a pass-first offense
kenneth walker iii.report: Walker managed just 11.3 PPG in 2025 with a modest 221 carries and weak advanced marks (8.3% target share, -0.84 rush EPA/g). The 273-point projection bets on a fresh, expanded role in Kansas City's high-scoring offense. Ceiling is a TD-fueled RB2 finish if he wins lead-back duties; floor is a committee where his limited receiving work hurts in PPR. The move to KC is the whole thesis; playoffs (NE, SF, @LAC) are middling.

javonte williams.verdict: Rebound to 14.3 PPG on real volume but poor -1.42 rec EPA; DAL committee threat looms
javonte williams.report: Williams bounced back to 14.3 PPG on 252 carries in 2025 after a dismal 2024, though his -1.42 rec EPA/g is alarming for a back who catches passes. Ceiling is a steady RB2 if he keeps the Dallas early-down and goal-line role. Floor is a committee outcome with rookie-type backs (Blue, Mafah) lurking and his pass-game efficiency crumbling. Low weekly variance (6.7 stdev) helps consistency; playoffs (@LAR, JAX, NYG) are decent.

kyren williams.verdict: Ultra-consistent volume back but low ceiling and rising Blake Corum/Hunter competition
kyren williams.report: Kyren is a metronome — 15.5 PPG on 259 carries in 2025 with a tiny 5.9 stdev and positive rush/rec EPA. Ceiling is limited by an 8% target share and the lowest projection (232) of the workhorse tier. Floor is solid thanks to guaranteed touches, but Blake Corum and rookie Jarquez Hunter are eating into the workload and the 2026 projection reflects that decline. He's a safe-but-flat RB2; playoff slate (DAL, @SEA, @TB) is neutral.

travis etienne jr..verdict: Bounced to 14.9 PPG in 2025 but on a new team (NO) with unclear role security
travis etienne jr..report: Etienne rebounded to 14.9 PPG on 260 carries in 2025 after a lost 2024 (7.7 PPG). Ceiling is a low-end RB2 if New Orleans hands him the lead role and receiving work. Floor is uncertain given the team change and murky depth situation. His low weekly variance is a plus, but the projection (241) signals modest expectations; playoff schedule (@TB, ARI, @ATL) is average.

cam skattebo.verdict: Flashed receiving chops in 8 games but Questionable tag and Tracy/Singletary committee cloud him
cam skattebo.report: Skattebo showed a useful receiving role (12.9% target share, 0.19 WOPR) across just eight games in 2025 but the -1.51 rush EPA/g and 7.5 PPG raw output are underwhelming. Ceiling is a lead role in the Giants backfield if he stays healthy and beats out Tyrone Tracy. Floor is low given the Questionable injury tag and a crowded depth chart. High variance (9.7 stdev) on limited snaps; playoffs (CLE, @DET, @DAL) are tough late.

quinshon judkins.verdict: Rookie lead back on a weak CLE offense with ugly -1.79 rush EPA; efficiency and QB play are drags
quinshon judkins.report: Judkins carried a heavy rookie load (230 carries, 26 catches) but produced only 10.0 PPG with a grim -1.79 rush EPA/g in Cleveland's struggling offense. Ceiling is a second-year efficiency jump if the Browns' scoring environment improves and he holds the job over Sampson. Floor is low given the poor offense and TD scarcity. He owns the workload but the situation caps upside; playoffs (@NYG, @BAL, IND) include a very tough Week 16.

bucky irving.verdict: Talented lead back but 2025 was a huge step back — injury and Gainwell target vampire are real red flags
bucky irving.report: Irving cratered from 14.4 PPG in 2024 to 8.1 in 2025, playing through injury (only 10 games of clean advanced data) with an ugly -3.56 rush EPA/g. His 2024 form shows a genuine three-down ceiling, but Kenny Gainwell exploded for 73 receptions and 16.3% target share, capping Bucky's passing-game upside. He remains the clear RB1 with workhorse volume when healthy, and the wk17 LAR matchup is fine, but 'Questionable' tag plus a receiving committee lowers the floor. Draft him on 2024 talent while accepting real 2025 warning signs.

treveyon henderson.verdict: Rookie posted 206 PPR on efficient dual-threat usage; ascending workhorse with Stevenson still lurking
treveyon henderson.report: Henderson delivered 12.1 PPG over a full 17 games as a rookie with positive rush (0.50) and rec (0.16) EPA, a strong efficiency profile to build on. His 180 carries and 35 catches signal an every-down role, and Year 2 leaps are common for backs with this usage. The floor risk is Rhamondre Stevenson vulturing goal-line and early-down work, keeping this a slight timeshare. Playoff slate (@KC, @NYJ, DEN) is middling, but the arrow points up.

d'andre swift.verdict: Boring, bankable volume — 223 carries, positive rush EPA, and minimal backfield threat in Chicago
d'andre swift.report: Swift has been remarkably steady, posting 12.6 then 13.4 PPG with 253 and 223 carries in back-to-back full seasons, and his 0.97 rush EPA/g in 2025 shows the offense trusts him. Low weekly stdev (7.1) makes him a reliable RB2 floor play with 73 first downs signaling real usage. Kyle Monangai is a fringe threat but not a true committee partner yet. Tough wk15 @BUF but GB/DET close the fantasy playoffs acceptably.

david montgomery.verdict: Efficient goal-line grinder but Woody Marks committee and receiving fade cap the ceiling
david montgomery.report: Montgomery slipped from 13.0 to 9.8 PPG as his role narrowed (185 to 158 carries, target share down to 5.4%). He's a TD-dependent early-down back with little passing work, which makes him volatile in PPR. Woody Marks emerged as a real change-of-pace threat, limiting Montgomery's snap ceiling in Houston. Reasonable floor as a starter but capped upside; wk16 @PHI is a rough playoff matchup.

bhayshul tuten.verdict: Explosive sophomore with clear RB1 depth chart but zero proven volume or receiving role
bhayshul tuten.report: Tuten managed just 5.2 PPG on 83 carries as a rookie with a dismal -0.68 rush EPA/g and a tiny 3.0% target share. He's atop a soft Jacksonville depth chart (Rodriguez, aging Abdullah) so opportunity could balloon in Year 2. The ceiling is genuine breakout if he seizes the lead role, but the floor is a full committee bust given how little he produced. Pure upside dart with a fine wk15 @HOU/wk17 WSH playoff pairing.

tony pollard.verdict: High-volume but hyper-inefficient (-1.28 rush EPA); floor play with almost no explosive upside
tony pollard.report: Pollard logged 242 carries and 33 catches but his -1.28 rush and -0.70 rec EPA/g reveal empty volume producing just 10.9 PPG. He's the clear Tennessee lead back with low weekly variance (5.5 stdev), giving a safe-ish floor. However Tyjae Spears and rookie depth threaten passing-down work, and the negative efficiency caps any breakout. A steady RB3 with limited ceiling in a poor offense.

jadarian price.verdict: Rookie with RB1 label in Seattle but Charbonnet blocks the workload — total projection
jadarian price.report: Price has no NFL data and sits atop the depth chart, but Zach Charbonnet is a proven, established back who will command real touches. The ceiling is a surprise rookie ascension into a lead role, but the realistic floor is a backup competing for scraps. The projection of 194 looks optimistic given the competition. Speculative late pick; wk15 @PHI is a tough playoff draw.

rico dowdle.verdict: Quietly produced 216 PPR as a workhorse; now RB1 in Pittsburgh but Warren splits touches
rico dowdle.report: Dowdle backed up 2024's 198 points with 216 in 2025 (12.7 PPG), pairing 236 carries with 39 catches and 65 first downs — legitimate three-down volume. His neutral EPA marks suggest volume-driven rather than elite efficiency, but the usage is real. Jaylen Warren is a genuine committee partner in Pittsburgh, so expect a split rather than a bell-cow. Solid RB2/3 value at his ADP with a manageable playoff slate.

jaylen warren.verdict: Efficient dual-threat (0.67 rec EPA) but now the RB2 behind Dowdle — usage will shrink
jaylen warren.report: Warren broke out to 12.8 PPG in 2025 on 211 carries and 40 catches with strong receiving efficiency, a big jump from 2024's part-time 7.3. The problem is the depth chart lists him behind Rico Dowdle, signaling a reduced or split role going forward. If he keeps the passing-down work his PPR floor holds, but a true timeshare caps the ceiling. Same PIT playoff schedule (BAL, CAR, @TEN) — decent middle weeks.

chuba hubbard.verdict: 2025 collapse (7.4 PPG) after a 242-point 2024; Brooks return clouds the lead role
chuba hubbard.report: Hubbard fell off a cliff from 14.2 PPG in 2024 to 7.4 in 2025 with a poor -1.04 rush EPA/g, though injury (15 games) played a part. He's still the listed Carolina RB1 with three-down capability shown in 2024. The wildcard is Jonathon Brooks returning to health, which could turn this into a committee or worse. Boom-bust flier with a real bounce-back ceiling but a scary floor; early wk5 bye and CIN/@PIT playoff draws are neutral.

aaron jones sr..verdict: Age and injury cratered 2025 to 7.0 PPG; no clear depth-chart data adds uncertainty
aaron jones sr..report: Jones plummeted from 14.2 PPG in 2024 to 7.0 in 2025 as injuries limited his effectiveness in Minnesota. The receiving chops (51 catches in 2024) remain a PPR asset if healthy, but the decline and age trend are alarming. Missing depth-chart data adds risk about his 2026 role and touch share. Projection of 189 feels aggressive; treat as a bounce-back gamble with a low floor.

kenny gainwell.verdict: 73 catches and 16.3% target share make him a sneaky PPR floor even as the TB RB2
kenny gainwell.report: Gainwell exploded to 13.0 PPG and a 0.23 WOPR on 85 targets — elite receiving-back usage that translates directly to PPR points. His 2024 was a nothing season, so the volume is unproven to repeat, and he sits behind Bucky Irving on the depth chart. If Bucky stays healthy Gainwell reverts to a passing-down role, but that role alone floats a decent floor and his 2025 form gives standalone RB2 upside if Bucky misses time. Underrated PPR value late.

rj harvey.verdict: Elite receiving efficiency (1.12 rec EPA/g) as a rookie but stuck behind Dobbins early-down work
rj harvey.report: Harvey posted 12.2 PPG and 47 catches as a rookie with a standout 1.12 rec EPA/g, flashing genuine passing-game talent. His -1.35 rush EPA/g shows the ground work isn't there yet, and he's listed RB2 behind J.K. Dobbins. The ceiling is taking over the Denver backfield outright if Dobbins fades or gets hurt — a real possibility given Dobbins' injury history. Upside handcuff with standalone PPR value.

j.k. dobbins.verdict: Only 6.8 PPG and 10 clean games in 2025; Harvey threatens the whole timeshare
j.k. dobbins.report: Dobbins declined to 6.8 PPG in an injury-shortened 2025 with a paltry 4.6% target share, a far cry from 2024's 11.3. He's the listed Denver RB1 but rookie RJ Harvey clearly outproduced him in efficiency and receiving. The persistent injury history (10 games again) makes the floor precarious. Volume-based upside exists if he holds the lead role, but this is a shaky committee at best.

rachaad white.verdict: Receiving skills intact but demoted to WSH RB2 behind Croskey-Merritt — role is the question
rachaad white.report: White's production dipped to 8.4 PPG in 2025 as his role shrank, though he retains PPR value via 40 catches and pass-down usage. He's now listed behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt on the Washington depth chart, capping his rushing volume. If he wins the passing-down role his PPR floor holds, but a true committee limits upside. Speculative late-round flier dependent on how the backfield sorts out.

kyle monangai.verdict: Rookie posted 8.6 PPG in a backup role; valuable Swift handcuff but limited standalone value
kyle monangai.report: Monangai flashed as a rookie with 169 carries and 8.6 PPG, showing he can handle volume if pressed into duty. He's firmly the RB2 behind D'Andre Swift, so standalone value is thin barring injury. As Swift's direct handcuff in a solid Chicago offense, he carries strong contingent upside. Draft as insurance/upside stash rather than a weekly starter.

jacory croskey-merritt.verdict: Nominal WSH RB1 as a rookie but tiny target share and negative rush EPA cap the outlook
jacory croskey-merritt.report: Croskey-Merritt logged 175 carries and 8.3 PPG as a rookie but did almost nothing in the passing game (3.0% target share, 0.04 WOPR) with a -0.38 rush EPA/g. He's listed atop the Washington depth chart, which gives lead-back upside if he consolidates the role. The floor is low given the crowded backfield with Rachaad White and others. Volume-dependent flier with modest PPR ceiling.

jonathon brooks.verdict: Talented but injury-wrecked with no recent data; pure upside stash behind Hubbard
jonathon brooks.report: Brooks has no usable 2024 or 2025 data after injuries derailed his career start, making his 2026 outlook entirely projection. He's listed RB2 behind Chuba Hubbard, but Hubbard's 2025 collapse leaves the door open for a role. The ceiling is a former high draft pick seizing lead duties in Carolina; the floor is another lost season. Deep-league dart throw only.

blake corum.verdict: Efficient runner (0.94 rush EPA) but locked behind Kyren Williams as pure handcuff
blake corum.report: Corum improved to 7.2 PPG in 2025 with a solid 0.94 rush EPA/g on 145 carries, showing he can produce when given work. He's the clear RB2 behind Kyren Williams with almost no passing role (2.3% target share), so standalone value is minimal. As Kyren's handcuff in a good Rams offense, he'd have immediate RB2 value if pressed into a lead role. Draft as insurance with league-winning contingent upside.

woody marks.verdict: Sophomore who logged 196 carries as HOU's RB2; standalone flex with real handcuff upside behind Montgomery
woody marks.report: Marks produced 151 PPR points on 196 carries and 24 catches in his rookie year, a genuine committee role rather than a pure backup. His rush EPA/g of -1.82 and 6.8% target share show the efficiency is poor, so the standalone value is touch-driven and capped while Montgomery holds the lead. If Montgomery (age/injury history) misses time, Marks becomes a clear RB2. Playoff slate is rough with @PHI and @GB in weeks 16-17.

jordan mason.verdict: Efficient, proven bell-cow-when-needed behind aging Aaron Jones; low-cost RB with contingent RB1 upside
jordan mason.report: Mason has two straight seasons near 150+ carries and improved to 129 points in 2025 with tight weekly variance (stdev 5.5). His pass-game role is minimal (3.5% target share, WOPR 0.04), which caps PPR ceiling unless he inherits the backfield. Aaron Jones' age and durability make Mason one of the better bet-on-injury handcuffs in this range. Mixed playoff draw (DET, WSH, @NYJ).

zach charbonnet.verdict: Two years of 180+ PPR points as a backup; league-winning ceiling if he takes the job, but PUP flag lingers
zach charbonnet.report: Charbonnet has posted 187 and 181 PPR points in back-to-back seasons despite backup billing, showing genuine three-down ability with 20-42 catches. The confusing depth chart and his PUP designation are the risk — health and role must clarify. If he wins early-down and passing work he's a top-24 back; if buried he's a bye-week fill-in. Tough week-15 draw @PHI.

tyrone tracy jr..verdict: Back-to-back 160+ point seasons with 10.8% target share; strong dual-threat profile despite murky roster
tyrone tracy jr..report: Tracy has been quietly productive, scoring 182 then 161 PPR points on heavy volume (176 carries, 48 targets in 2025) with a healthy 0.16 WOPR. His rush EPA/g of -0.65 shows the efficiency is shaky, so continued production depends on the Giants funneling him touches. The projection of 80 signals expected competition or a reduced role, making this a bet on volume holding. He's a discount if he retains the workhorse job.

tyjae spears.verdict: Highest projection in the group (149) on a pass-catching role; PPR-friendly floor behind Pollard
tyjae spears.report: Spears is a target magnet out of the backfield (50 targets, 45 catches, 12.3% target share in 2025) which stabilizes his PPR floor even with only 72 carries. The negative air-yards share and modest rushing role cap his ceiling unless Pollard misses time and he absorbs early downs. His receiving profile makes him startable in deeper PPR formats week to week. Reasonable playoff schedule (IND, @LV, PIT).

alvin kamara.verdict: Fell off a cliff in 2025 (5.9 ppg) at age-9 wear; name value only, chasing a lost season
alvin kamara.report: Kamara collapsed from 265 PPR points in 2024 to just 101 across an injury-shortened, ineffective 2025, with brutal rush EPA/g of -2.62. The 11.7% target share hints he can still catch passes, but the burst and efficiency are gone and he's now behind Etienne on the depth chart. Floor is a low-end committee back; ceiling requires a health-and-role rebound that the data doesn't support. Draft only as a late dart.

justice hill.verdict: Pure passing-down back with 10% target share; PPR sneaky-relevant when Baltimore trails or Henry rests
justice hill.report: Hill's value is entirely receiving — 51 then 27 targets with almost no carries (18 in 2025) behind Derrick Henry. His 0.15 WOPR and pass-game role give him a usable PPR floor in a strong offense, but the 7.0 weekly stdev shows boom-bust dependence on game script. Henry's age gives a contingency path to more carries. A bench stash with matchup-based flex weeks.

isiah pacheco.verdict: Now the clear No. 2 behind Gibbs in DET; usage cratered, standalone value limited
isiah pacheco.report: Pacheco's production slid to 87 points and his efficiency was poor (rush EPA/g -1.05) even before landing behind Jahmyr Gibbs. As a change-of-pace in Detroit he'll see early-down and goal-line work but no receiving volume to prop up PPR. Floor is a touchdown-dependent flex; ceiling comes only if Gibbs misses time. Bench depth at this cost.

braelon allen.verdict: Handcuff to Breece Hall with genuine lead-back upside, but 2025 was a lost, injury-marred year
braelon allen.report: Allen managed just 15 points across 4 effective games in 2025 after a promising 85-point rookie campaign. The talent and size make him the direct beneficiary if Breece Hall is dealt or hurt, which is the entire draft case. Standalone role is negligible right now, so this is a pure contingency stash. Playoff schedule is fine (@ARI, NE, MIN).

tank bigsby.verdict: Traded to PHI behind Saquon; premier handcuff spot but zero standalone touches
tank bigsby.report: Bigsby's role vanished in 2025 (54 points, 1.2% target share) and now he sits behind Saquon Barkley in Philadelphia. The appeal is purely the handcuff: if Barkley misses time, Bigsby steps into an elite rushing environment. As long as Saquon is healthy he's undraftable in most formats. New team, unproven role.

tyler allgeier.verdict: Steady early-down grinder now behind rookie Love in ARI; touchdown-dependent depth
tyler allgeier.report: Allgeier has been remarkably consistent (106 then 123 points, low stdev) as a physical committee back, but his 3.2% target share offers no PPR safety net. The move to a Jeremiyah Love-led backfield in Arizona likely relegates him to short-yardage and change-up work. Floor is a bye-week filler; ceiling requires a Love injury to unlock carries. Late bench pick.

jordan james.verdict: Second-year back behind CMC; the McCaffrey injury lottery ticket is the whole appeal
jordan james.report: James has no NFL production yet but sits as the clear No. 2 behind Christian McCaffrey in a productive Shanahan scheme. That backfield has repeatedly turned backups into fantasy starters, so his contingent ceiling is significant. With CMC healthy he's a non-factor, making this a boom-or-nothing stash. Tough playoff slate (@LAC, @KC).

chris rodriguez jr..verdict: Grinding rushing role in JAX with almost no passing work; low, touchdown-dependent floor
chris rodriguez jr..report: Rodriguez managed 92 points on 112 carries with a positive rush EPA/g (0.52), a rare bright spot, but caught only 3 passes. That non-existent receiving role kills his PPR value and makes him touchdown-reliant. Uncertain roster standing keeps him a deep-league-only name. Little standalone upside without a role expansion.

brian robinson jr..verdict: New team in ATL behind Bijan; role collapsed in 2025 and no path to volume
brian robinson jr..report: Robinson's production fell off a cliff from 160 points in 2024 to 63 in 2025 as his role evaporated. Landing in Atlanta behind Bijan Robinson offers little standalone opportunity beyond short-yardage vulture work. Floor is minimal and the ceiling caps out as a bye-week desperation start. Draft only in the deepest formats.

ray davis.verdict: Buried as BUF RB4 behind Cook and Johnson; solid handcuff-of-a-handcuff only
ray davis.report: Davis was efficient in his limited work (positive rush and rec EPA/g) but the 2025 role shrank to 64 points behind James Cook. As the fourth listed back in Buffalo, he needs multiple injuries to matter, though the offense's scoring environment gives contingent upside. Standalone value is near zero. Deep-stash only.

keaton mitchell.verdict: Explosive but tiny-role change-of-pace behind Hampton in LAC; injury-prone flier
keaton mitchell.report: Mitchell offers big-play speed but managed only 55 points and a poor rec EPA/g (-0.43) in 2025 while battling health. He sits behind Omarion Hampton and profiles as a spark-plug rather than a volume back. Ceiling is a few explosive weeks; floor is irrelevance if Hampton stays healthy. Waiver-priority type more than a draft pick.

mike washington jr..verdict: Unknown rookie/return in LV with no data and unclear roster spot; pure dart throw
mike washington jr..report: Washington has no available production data and no clear depth-chart footprint, making projection speculative. The 65-point projection suggests some expected role, but without usage or advanced metrics there's nothing to anchor confidence. This is a last-round flier on situation rather than proven ability. Monitor camp before rostering.

james conner.verdict: Projection of zero signals likely retirement/season-ending status; do not draft
james conner.report: Conner was a 254-point workhorse in 2024 but appeared in just 3 games in 2025 before his season ended, and his 2026 projection of 0 implies he's out of the picture. The advanced metrics from his brief 2025 sample were fine, but health and availability are the fatal issues at age-9 wear. There's no draftable case here. Avoid entirely.

kaelon black.verdict: Undrafted-caliber rookie RB3 behind CMC and James; contingency of a contingency
kaelon black.report: Black is a rookie with no data buried as the third back in San Francisco behind McCaffrey and Jordan James. He needs a cascade of injuries to see meaningful touches, though the scheme gives faint upside. Essentially undraftable outside 20-team dynasty formats. Watchlist only.

kaytron allen.verdict: Rookie RB4 in a crowded WSH backfield with a 16-point projection; not draftable
kaytron allen.report: Allen enters as the fourth listed back behind Croskey-Merritt, White, and McNichols with no NFL production. The 16-point projection reflects almost no expected role, and the path to touches is blocked by three names. There is no reason to spend a pick here in redraft. Dynasty-deep-stash at best.

nicholas singleton.verdict: Rookie buried at RB3 but talent and Pollard's age give real handcuff upside in TEN
nicholas singleton.report: No NFL data yet, but he lands as the #3 behind an aging Tony Pollard and oft-injured Tyjae Spears, so an early opportunity is plausible. The ceiling case is a mid-season promotion into a lead role if Pollard slows or misses time. The floor is near-zero standalone value buried on the depth chart with Carter and Mullings also present. A pure late-round dart with a bye in Week 9 and a manageable playoff slate.

demond claiborne.verdict: Rookie stashed behind Jones/Mason in MIN; needs an injury to matter but the room clears fast
demond claiborne.report: No prior data as a rookie sitting at RB3 behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason. Jones is aging and Mason has an injury profile, so a path to touches exists if the top two falter. The ceiling is a committee role in a good offense; the floor is inactive weeks and minimal usage. Draft only as a deep bench speculation.

jonah coleman.verdict: Rookie fourth-string-ish in a crowded DEN backfield with Dobbins, Harvey and others ahead
jonah coleman.report: No NFL production and a muddy depth chart featuring J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey and Jaleel McLaughlin ahead of him. The ceiling requires multiple injuries to clear the room, which caps realistic upside. Floor is essentially a redshirt with no fantasy relevance. Only a dynasty-flavored stash in redraft.

seth mcgowan.verdict: Third on IND's chart behind the workhorse Jonathan Taylor; lottery ticket at best
seth mcgowan.report: No data and stuck behind one of the league's premier bell cows in Jonathan Taylor plus DJ Giddens. The only path to value is a Taylor injury, which would spike his ceiling given Indy's run volume. The floor is total irrelevance in most weeks. Not worth a roster spot outside deep formats.

emmett johnson.verdict: Rookie RB3 in KC behind Walker and Demercado; pass-game role possible but crowded
emmett johnson.report: No prior production with Kenneth Walker atop the KC chart and Demercado, Smith and Ott also competing. The ceiling is a change-of-pace or receiving role in a high-powered Chiefs offense. The floor is a healthy scratch most weeks. A speculative late stash tied to Walker's durability.

dylan sampson.verdict: Proven rookie receiving chops (33 rec) as CLE RB2; strong handcuff to Judkins
dylan sampson.report: As a rookie he posted 88 PPR points with 33 catches and a positive receiving EPA (0.46/g), showing genuine pass-game value even in a backup role. His rush EPA (-1.12) was poor, so his standalone value leans receiving, but he's the clear handcuff to Quinshon Judkins. The ceiling is a near-workhorse line if Judkins misses time; the floor is flex-viable PPR points on catches alone. Tough Week 16 playoff matchup at Baltimore.

samaje perine.verdict: Veteran passing-down back behind Chase Brown; low ceiling, dependable but capped role
samaje perine.report: Two straight seasons of ~78-81 PPR points on a defined third-down role, with modest 4.1% target share in 2025. His usage is stable but unspectacular and firmly behind Chase Brown. The ceiling is a slight bump if Brown misses time in a good Bengals offense; the floor is his standard low-volume line. Minimal weekly upside makes him a deep-league only piece.

lequint allen jr..verdict: Minimal 2025 role (1.5 ppg) in JAX; negative EPA and no clear path to touches
lequint allen jr..report: Managed just 25 PPR points across a rookie season with tiny 2.1% target share and negative rushing and receiving EPA. Nothing in the usage suggests a coming breakout. The ceiling depends entirely on injuries ahead of him; the floor is irrelevance. A dart throw at best.

jaylen wright.verdict: Explosive but buried behind Achane and Gordon in MIA; ugly -0.63 rush EPA
jaylen wright.report: Two years of low production (2.8 and 1.6 ppg) with poor rush efficiency and almost no receiving role. He sits behind De'Von Achane and Ollie Gordon, limiting standalone value. The ceiling is a spike role if Achane misses time given his big-play ability; the floor is inactive weeks. Speculative handcuff.

ollie gordon ii.verdict: MIA's early-down grinder behind Achane; volume-based low ceiling, poor efficiency
ollie gordon ii.report: Played all 17 games for 54 points with 70 carries but weak efficiency (-0.56 rush EPA) and near-zero receiving role (1.8% target share). He's ahead of Wright as the between-the-tackles back, giving him first crack if Achane is out. The ceiling is a lead early-down role; the floor is spot duty. A better bet than Wright for pure carries if Achane misses time.

kimani vidal.verdict: Proven 8.4 ppg workload when given the LAC job; best upside dart in this cluster
kimani vidal.report: Vidal exploded to 118 PPR points in 14 games (8.4 ppg) on 155 carries when pressed into duty, showing he can carry a real workload. He now sits behind Omarion Hampton, but that makes him the single most valuable handcuff here given proven bell-cow usage in the Chargers' offense. The ceiling is RB2 numbers if Hampton misses extended time; the floor is limited standalone touches. His rush EPA was poor (-1.08) on high volume, a mild caution, but the opportunity profile is elite for this range.

adam randall.verdict: Rookie behind Derrick Henry; premium handcuff spot but Henry rarely misses
adam randall.report: No NFL data yet, landing at RB3 behind the durable Derrick Henry and pass-catching Justice Hill. The handcuff value is real because Henry's touches would be enormous if he ever missed time. The floor is zero standalone usage; the ceiling depends entirely on a Henry absence. A high-variance stash given Henry's age but reliability.

marshawn lloyd.verdict: Talented but oft-hurt GB back behind Jacobs; upside exists if he stays healthy
marshawn lloyd.report: Still no meaningful NFL data after injuries, sitting behind Josh Jacobs with Brooks (PUP) and others in the mix. The draft capital and athletic profile keep his ceiling alive as the primary handcuff to Jacobs. The floor is another lost or buried season. A boom-bust late-round flier.

emari demercado.verdict: Steady low-volume KC change-up; two years of ~3.3 ppg with a stable pass role
emari demercado.report: Consistent but small production (58 and 55 points) with a modest receiving role and negative rush EPA (-0.58). He's the RB2 behind Kenneth Walker, giving some contingent value in Kansas City's offense. The ceiling is flex weeks if Walker misses time; the floor is his usual spot duty. Better as an injury insurance piece than a standalone play.

jaydon blue.verdict: Explosive DAL rookie who flashed; buried at RB3 but athletic upside if room clears
jaydon blue.report: Only 20 points and a dreadful -1.50 rush EPA in a tiny 5-game sample, so the on-field results were rough. He sits at RB3 behind Javonte Williams, capping immediate opportunity. The ceiling is a receiving/change-of-pace role emerging in year two if injuries hit; the floor is inactive. Purely an upside dart on speed and draft pedigree.

trey benson.verdict: Projected zero and buried at RB5 in ARI after the Jeremiyah Love/Conner logjam
trey benson.report: A 2026 projection of 0 and RB5 designation signal he's essentially off the fantasy radar, stuck behind Jeremiyah Love, Allgeier and Conner. His 2025 was a lost 4-game sample with an alarming -2.02 receiving EPA. The floor is a healthy scratch; even the ceiling requires multiple injuries. Avoid outside the deepest formats.

kaleb johnson.verdict: Projected 5 points, RB4 in PIT after a lost rookie year; no path to touches
kaleb johnson.report: His 2025 usage was minimal with a -0.77 rush EPA and near-zero pass role, and he now sits fourth behind Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren. The projection of 5 points reflects a total lack of expected opportunity. The ceiling requires a cascade of injuries; the floor is irrelevance. Not draftable in standard leagues.

ty johnson.verdict: Elite receiving-back efficiency in BUF; standalone PPR value plus Cook handcuff upside
ty johnson.report: Two straight 90+ point seasons with excellent receiving EPA (0.67/g) and even positive rush EPA (0.16), a rare efficiency profile for a backup. He earns steady passing-down work in a high-scoring Buffalo offense, giving genuine floor value on catches alone. The ceiling spikes if James Cook misses time; the floor is a useful bye-week PPR flex. One of the safer picks in this range.

kyle juszczyk.verdict: Reliable fullback receiving role in SF but a hard scoring ceiling; not an RB play
kyle juszczyk.report: His value is entirely as a receiving fullback with 24 catches and positive receiving EPA (0.46/g), yielding stable but low ~57-point seasons. There's no carry volume (2 attempts) and thus no path to a spike week. The floor and ceiling are both narrow and low for fantasy purposes. Effectively a non-factor in standard PPR rosters.

chris brooks.verdict: PUP designation and RB2 role in GB cap value; low output even when active
chris brooks.report: Coming off PUP with modest career production (33 and 42 points) and negative rush EPA, his outlook is clouded by both health and depth. He's nominally the RB2 behind Josh Jacobs but competes with MarShawn Lloyd for that contingent role. The ceiling is limited flex value if Jacobs misses time; the floor is the PUP list. A low-priority stash.

george holani.verdict: Buried SEA RB4 with negative rush EPA and near-zero target share; pure roster filler
george holani.report: Holani managed just 0.9 PPG on 22 carries with a brutal -0.93 rush EPA/g and a 1.0% target share in 2025 — essentially replacement-level touches. He sits fourth on a crowded depth chart behind Jadarian Price, Zach Charbonnet and Emanuel Wilson, so a standalone role is nearly impossible barring a cascade of injuries. His ceiling only exists if multiple backs ahead of him miss time, and even then his advanced metrics say he does little with the work. The playoff slate (@PHI, @CAR) is unremarkable because he won't be startable regardless.

isaiah davis.verdict: Emerging NYJ pass-catching RB3 with a positive rec EPA and modest standalone flex appeal
isaiah davis.report: Davis nearly doubled his output year over year (2.7 to 4.2 PPG) while growing his target share to 6.3% and posting a healthy 0.29 rec EPA/g, a sign his passing-down role is real. He's stuck behind Breece Hall and Braelon Allen, capping standalone touches, but he'd be a valuable satellite piece if either misses time. Floor is low as a game-script-dependent RB3, but his receiving usage gives him a firmer PPR baseline than most players in this range. The wk17 MIN home matchup is fine but he needs an injury to be a difference-maker.

dj giddens.verdict: Sole handcuff to Jonathan Taylor in IND — best contingent ceiling in this entire tier
dj giddens.report: Giddens has minimal 2025 sample (5 games, tiny target share) but the value here is positional: he's the clear RB2 behind Jonathan Taylor with only Seth McGowan behind him. Any Taylor absence in a run-heavy Colts offense turns Giddens into a locked-in RB1/RB2 with three-down upside, the exact profile you draft at pick 276. His floor is near zero as long as Taylor is healthy, so this is a pure lottery ticket, but the payoff is the highest in the group. Playoff opponents (@TEN, CIN, @CLE) are neutral-to-favorable if he's forced into a lead role.

malik davis.verdict: DAL RB2 behind fragile Javonte with real carry volume but weak receiving profile
malik davis.report: Davis logged 52 carries and 3.7 PPG in a committee, with a slightly positive 0.08 rush EPA/g but almost no receiving involvement (1.4% target share, -0.48 rec EPA/g). Sitting second behind an injury-prone Javonte Williams gives him a plausible path to lead-back carries, though Jaydon Blue and others lurk to steal work. His floor is thin because he offers little in PPR unless he's the primary early-down runner. The Dallas backfield is muddy, so treat him as a wait-and-see stash with modest bell-cow-if-injury upside.

sean tucker.verdict: TB RB3 with a proven 86-carry season and explosive weekly ceiling behind injury-prone Irving
sean tucker.report: Tucker improved to 5.4 PPG on 86 carries with a high 8.0 weekly stdev, signaling boom-bust big-play ability when given volume. He sits behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell, but his handcuff-to-Irving standing in a competent offense gives him meaningful contingent value. Advanced metrics are lukewarm (negative rush and rec EPA), so his profile is more volume-and-explosiveness than efficiency. If Irving misses time, Tucker's flashes suggest RB2 upside; otherwise he's a spot-start dart with a firm handcuff floor.

trevor etienne.verdict: CAR RB4 stuck behind a full depth chart with negligible 2025 usage
trevor etienne.report: Etienne played all 17 games but produced just 0.7 PPG on 20 carries with a 0.6% target share — effectively invisible in the offense. He's fourth on the depth chart behind Chuba Hubbard, Jonathon Brooks and AJ Dillon, so his path to touches requires multiple injuries. His advanced numbers are near-neutral rather than actively bad, but there's simply no volume to project forward. A deep-league dart with almost no standalone value and a distant handcuff ceiling.

emanuel wilson.verdict: Two straight 95-point seasons on real volume make him the safest floor in this range
emanuel wilson.report: Wilson has quietly produced back-to-back ~95-point, 5.6-PPG seasons on 100+ carries and double-digit receptions, giving him the most established weekly usage of anyone here. His rush EPA/g of -0.45 is poor, but the sheer volume (125 carries, 37 first downs) delivers usable PPR flex weeks. He's listed as a committee back with a defined role, so his floor is the highest in the group even if his ceiling is capped without a bump in touches. The projection of just 10 points looks conservative given his actual usage — a value at this ADP.

will shipley.verdict: PHI RB5 on paper but the true handcuff to elite Saquon — high-variance lottery ticket
will shipley.report: Shipley's raw numbers are tiny (1.0 PPG, 14 carries) with a soft 2.9% target share and negative EPA, reflecting near-zero role behind Saquon Barkley. The listed depth chart buries him at RB5, but reality is he profiles as the primary backup in one of the league's best rushing offenses. That makes his contingent ceiling enormous if Barkley misses time, even though his standalone floor is basically nothing. This is a boom-if-injury handcuff bet, nothing more, with a favorable wk15 SEA playoff matchup should he inherit the role.

devin singletary.verdict: Highest actual scorer here (6.4 PPG) but veteran now behind Skattebo and Tracy on NYG
devin singletary.report: Singletary posted the group's best output at 6.4 PPG with 119 carries and 18 receptions, plus a respectable 0.13 rec EPA/g and 31 first downs — a genuinely useful all-around season. The problem is forward-looking role: he's now listed RB3 behind Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy, so that volume is unlikely to repeat at age-adjusted, seven-year-vet status. His floor is buoyed by pass-game reliability, but the ceiling is compressed by a younger, ascending depth chart. Bet on the receiving floor for bye-week fill, not a return to featured touches.

hunter luepke.verdict: Pass-catching DAL fullback with a sneaky 0.33 rec EPA/g but almost no rushing role
hunter luepke.report: Luepke is a receiving specialist, growing to a 3.3% target share and an excellent 0.33 rec EPA/g, but with just 16 carries his rushing upside is minimal. As a hybrid FB/RB he offers a niche PPR floor via checkdowns rather than any bell-cow potential. His ceiling is capped unless Dallas dramatically expands his role, which the usage trend doesn't support. Best viewed as a deep-league receiving dart with a stable-but-low weekly baseline.

puka nacua.verdict: Elite target monster with 30% share and 0.69 WOPR; only Adams' arrival caps the absolute ceiling
puka nacua.report: Nacua exploded to 22.1 PPG in 2025 on a monster 30.1% target share, 33.7% air-yards share and 0.69 WOPR — that's genuine alpha usage, not TD luck given his 7.23 rec EPA/game. The ceiling is the overall WR1 if that volume holds. The floor case is Davante Adams siphoning red-zone and secondary looks now that he's the clear #2 in LA. Playoff slate (DAL, @SEA, @TB) is neutral; the volume is what makes him a top-3 lock.

ja'marr chase.verdict: 32% target share and 0.74 WOPR make him a weekly ceiling play even off a slightly down 2025
ja'marr chase.report: Chase dipped from a monster 2024 (403 pts) to a still-elite 314 in 2025, but the underlying usage only got stronger — 32.1% target share, 36.6% air-yards share, 0.74 WOPR. The ceiling is a return to the overall WR1 spot Burrow enables. Floor risk is Tee Higgins eating into TD equity and Burrow's health as the offense's linchpin. Week 17 vs BAL is the only tough playoff draw; otherwise the schedule is fine.

jaxon smith-njigba.verdict: Absurd 0.90 WOPR and 50% air-yards share — the most dominant usage profile in the entire group
jaxon smith-njigba.report: JSN's 2025 leap (360 pts, 21.2 PPG) was backed by a jaw-dropping 36.8% target share, 50.4% air-yards share and 0.90 WOPR — he is effectively the entire Seattle passing tree. His low 7.3 weekly stdev makes him the safest ceiling-plus-floor combo here. The only floor concern is Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed potentially reclaiming a few targets, but nothing in the data suggests a real threat. A must-draft top-5 WR.

amon-ra st. brown.verdict: Metronomic 19 PPG on 31.7% share; the safest floor at the position with WR1 upside
amon-ra st. brown.report: St. Brown has posted 316 and 324 points in back-to-back years with a 31.7% target share and 0.75 WOPR — elite, sustainable volume in a high-scoring Detroit offense. His ceiling is capped slightly by Jameson Williams stealing big plays, but his floor is the best in this tier given the target consistency. Slot usage keeps him healthy and involved. Playoff draw (@MIN, NYG, @CHI) is favorable.

ceedee lamb.verdict: Down, injury-shortened 2025 and Pickens' arrival cap the ceiling, but the talent floor is high
ceedee lamb.report: Lamb slumped to 11.8 PPG in an injury-limited 13-game 2025, with target share dropping to 25.1% and WOPR to 0.61 as George Pickens emerged alongside him. The bounce-back ceiling exists if he reclaims the 152-target 2024 role, but that's now genuinely contested. The floor is a low-end WR1/high WR2 splitting the offense. Week 15 @LAR is a tough playoff spot.

justin jefferson.verdict: Elite volume trapped in a broken 2025 passing game; -0.81 rec EPA/g is a giant red flag
justin jefferson.report: Jefferson kept his usage (30.7% target share, 0.74 WOPR) but production cratered to 11.9 PPG as the QB situation collapsed — his -0.81 rec EPA/game is alarming and QB-driven, not talent-driven. If Minnesota's quarterback play rebounds, he's a top-5 ceiling talent. The floor is another frustrating year of empty volume like 2025. His remarkably low 5.6 stdev in 2025 shows how muted the offense was.

drake london.verdict: Alpha usage when healthy (0.73 WOPR) but a Questionable tag and boom-bust 12.0 stdev
drake london.report: London carried a 29.7% target share and 0.73 WOPR across just 12 games in 2025 — elite per-game opportunity undermined by availability and a wild 12.0 weekly stdev. The ceiling is a top-8 WR if he plays 17 and the Atlanta offense clicks. The floor is real given the injury flag and his TD-dependent volatility. Little target competition on the depth chart, so health is the whole story.

rashee rice.verdict: 8-game sample screams volume (29% share) in KC's offense; suspension/availability is the risk
rashee rice.report: In just 8 games Rice commanded a 29.0% target share and produced efficiently (2.00 rec EPA/g) as Mahomes' clear top target. Full-season projection of 270 reflects genuine WR1 upside if he stays on the field for 17. The floor is availability risk and Xavier Worthy cutting into the workload. His low air-yards share (13.7%) means he's a volume-and-YAC play rather than a downfield one, capping ceiling slightly.

nico collins.verdict: Steady 0.61 WOPR alpha in Houston but rising rookie competition tempers the ceiling
nico collins.report: Collins posted 226 points on a 24.2% target share and solid 2.62 rec EPA/game, remaining Houston's clear WR1. The ceiling is a mid-WR1 finish if the offense takes a step. The floor concern is Jayden Higgins and a healthy Tank Dell eroding his 24% share below the level needed for weekly WR1 upside. Low stdev (7.6) makes him a reliable WR2 with modest ceiling.

garrett wilson.verdict: 0.92 WOPR in 7 games shows total alpha usage; injury-shortened 2025 is a buy-low
garrett wilson.report: Wilson's 2025 was wrecked by injury (7 games, 5.9 PPG) but the underlying usage was absurd — 35.4% target share, 56.3% air-yards share, 0.92 WOPR. Healthy, that's a 2024-caliber (252-point) profile with even more concentration. The ceiling is a top-10 WR; the floor is the QB situation and the -0.30 rec EPA/game hinting at poor quarterback play. Weak WR room means all the volume is his.

a.j. brown.verdict: Steady 0.68 WOPR alpha but a new team in New England adds real projection uncertainty
a.j. brown.report: Brown quietly posted 220 points on a 28.7% target share in 2025 and remains a true WR1 talent, now the clear top option in New England. The ceiling depends entirely on his new QB and system elevating his volume. The floor is a transition-year dip if the offense sputters. Week 15 @KC and the AFC playoff slate are middling; the new-team unknown is the main deduction here.

chris olave.verdict: Full, healthy 2025 (268 pts, 29% share) makes him a rock-solid WR2 with WR1 upside
chris olave.report: Olave rebounded from a lost 2024 to a genuinely strong 2025 — 268 points, 29.2% target share, 0.72 WOPR and 41% air-yards share as New Orleans' clear alpha. The ceiling is a low-end WR1 if the QB play supports it. The floor is the shaky Saints offense limiting scoring and his history of concussions. Playoff schedule (@TB, ARI, @ATL) is manageable.

george pickens.verdict: Big 2025 (292 pts) but only 22.5% share alongside Lamb makes him a high-variance #2
george pickens.report: Pickens broke out for 17.2 PPG and elite 5.22 rec EPA/game in 2025, but he did it on just a 22.5% target share and 0.56 WOPR — a lower-volume, big-play profile now sharing Dallas with CeeDee Lamb. The ceiling is another efficient top-15 season if the deep balls keep landing. The floor is TD-and-explosive-play dependency regressing next to a healthy Lamb. Genuine touch competition caps the upside.

tetairoa mcmillan.verdict: Rookie-year 46% air-yards share signals a Year-2 breakout as Carolina's clear alpha
tetairoa mcmillan.report: McMillan's rookie season (211 pts, 25.7% target share, huge 45.9% air-yards share) established him as Carolina's undisputed WR1 with downfield alpha usage. The ceiling is a Year-2 leap into WR1 territory if Carolina's offense and QB improve. The floor is a stagnant offense and modest 1.49 rec EPA/game holding him at low-WR2. Minimal target competition on the roster is a plus.

zay flowers.verdict: Consistent 30% share plus rushing usage in a strong offense; capped ceiling but safe floor
zay flowers.report: Flowers delivered 243 points on a 29.9% target share and 0.70 WOPR, adding 10 carries for extra floor in Baltimore's efficient offense. His low 7.3 stdev makes him a dependable WR2. The ceiling is limited by a run-heavy scheme that suppresses passing volume, and the floor is solid given his entrenched role. Week 15 @PIT and 17 @CIN are tougher playoff matchups.

devonta smith.verdict: Reliable but volume-capped WR2 (0.59 WOPR) in a run-first, target-scarce Philadelphia offense
devonta smith.report: Smith has posted ~200 points three years running with a modest 24.6% target share and 0.59 WOPR — the Eagles' run-heavy, spread-the-ball offense limits his upside. His 3.20 rec EPA/game shows he's efficient with what he gets. The ceiling is a low-end WR1 in a shootout-heavy year; the floor is another steady but unspectacular WR2/3 line. A safe, low-variance pick with a hard ceiling.

emeka egbuka.verdict: Solid rookie volume (127 tgt) but Godwin's return and 0.42 rec EPA/g cap the near-term ceiling
emeka egbuka.report: Egbuka logged a full 17-game rookie season with 127 targets and a 23.6% share, showing he can command volume. The ceiling is a Year-2 step if Tampa leans on him, but a healthy Chris Godwin returning directly competes for slot/underneath work. His weak 0.42 rec EPA/game suggests the efficiency needs to catch up to the volume. A back-end WR3 with modest upside.

malik nabers.verdict: Only 4 games in 2025 but 2024 alpha usage (170 tgt) makes him a high-ceiling injury bounce-back
malik nabers.report: Nabers' 2025 was lost to injury after just 4 games, but his 2024 (274 pts, 170 targets, 16.1 PPG) and the 27.1% share / 0.71 WOPR he flashed in his brief 2025 sample confirm elite alpha usage. The ceiling is a top-10 WR if fully healthy — he's the entire Giants passing game. The floor is significant given the Questionable tag and shaky QB play. A boom-or-bust swing at ADP.

davante adams.verdict: Still productive (223 pts) but now the clear #2 behind Nacua in LA at age 33+
davante adams.report: Adams posted a solid 223 points on a 25.1% target share in 2025, but joining the Rams as the #2 behind Puka Nacua caps his volume ceiling meaningfully. He remains a red-zone and route-running weapon with a decent 1.93 rec EPA/game. The ceiling is a WR2 finish if the Rams throw enough to feed two mouths; the floor is age-related decline and target compression. Shares the same neutral playoff slate as Nacua.

ladd mcconkey.verdict: Efficiency dipped and usage thinned (0.50 WOPR, 21% share); a Questionable tag adds floor risk
ladd mcconkey.report: McConkey regressed from 241 to 181 points as his target share fell to 21.1% and WOPR to a mediocre 0.50 with a poor 0.45 rec EPA/game. The ceiling is a rebound to his 2024 form if the Chargers funnel targets back to him. The floor is real given the injury flag and a crowded room with Johnston and Harris. Week 17 vs KC is a tough playoff finish. A WR3 dart with limited upside.

terry mclaurin.verdict: Elite 2024 form and 0.61 WOPR make him a buy-low bounce-back if health cooperates
terry mclaurin.report: 2024 was a true alpha season (268 pts, 15.8 PPG, 117 targets) before 2025 cratered to 6.7 PPG across an injury-shortened, disjointed year. The advanced numbers over his 10 games (23.2% target share, 37.1% air-yards, 0.61 WOPR, 3.17 rec EPA/g) confirm the target monopoly is intact when he plays, so the collapse reads as circumstance/health not skill decline. He's the clear WR1 in Washington with weak competition (Williams, Brown), giving a high ceiling. The floor is scary given the 2025 games-missed risk and QB uncertainty, and the wk16 @MIN / wk17 @JAX playoff slate is only average.

tee higgins.verdict: Most stable WR2 in the group with elite QB and a reliable 12-13 PPG floor
tee higgins.report: Two straight seasons of 12-13 PPG (212 and 222 pts) with a strong 41 first downs and 2.40 rec EPA/g in 2025 make him the safest bet here. The 18.3% target share and 0.50 WOPR are capped by Chase's dominance, but tying his production to Burrow's offense raises his weekly ceiling every game. Floor is high because volume and red-zone role are secure; ceiling is limited by being the clear WR2. Wk17 vs BAL is a tough finish but wk15 @CAR / wk16 @IND are plus matchups.

jameson williams.verdict: Back-to-back 12.5+ PPG in a loaded offense with a rising 3.30 rec EPA/g
jameson williams.report: Two consecutive productive years (212 then 220 pts, 12.5-12.9 PPG) with growing target volume (91 to 102) show real, repeatable WR2 value behind Amon-Ra St. Brown. The 18.6% target share and 0.50 WOPR are modest but the 3.30 rec EPA/g and 49 first downs reflect explosive, efficient usage plus a rushing package (6 carries). Ceiling comes from big-play upside in a top offense; floor is supported by full 17-game availability both seasons. Playoff slate is fine (wk16 vs NYG soft, wk15 @MIN and wk17 @CHI tougher).

jaylen waddle.verdict: Rising usage (0.65 WOPR) but a new Denver home creates target-competition questions
jaylen waddle.report: 2025 was a clear step forward (194 pts, 11.4 PPG, 100 targets, 23.3% share, 42.7% air-yards, 0.65 WOPR) after a down 2024. That elite opportunity profile is encouraging, but he now shares Denver with Courtland Sutton, the established WR1, which caps the ceiling and muddies the target hierarchy. Floor is solid given his target volume; ceiling depends on winning the pecking order in a new scheme. Playoff schedule is manageable (wk15 @LV, wk17 @NE) aside from wk16 vs BUF.

courtland sutton.verdict: Rock-steady WR1 volume (52 first downs, 0.56 WOPR) even with Waddle arriving
courtland sutton.report: Two straight strong years (240 then 220 pts, ~13-14 PPG) with a full 17 games and a robust 2025 profile (21.1% target share, 34.4% air-yards, 0.56 WOPR, 52 first downs, 2.68 rec EPA/g). He's the incumbent alpha, but Waddle's arrival introduces real target competition that could shave his ceiling. Floor is high thanks to red-zone volume and consistency (7.3 stdev); ceiling is a low-end WR1 finish. Playoff slate is neutral-to-good with wk15 @LV and wk17 @NE.

dk metcalf.verdict: Consistent 11 PPG deep threat now anchoring a rebuilt Pittsburgh receiver room
dk metcalf.report: Remarkably steady across two years (191 then 187 pts, ~11 PPG, low 6.8-7.2 stdev) with a strong 2025 usage profile (22.4% target share, 37.2% air-yards, 0.60 WOPR). As Pittsburgh's clear WR1 with only Pittman as real competition, his target floor is secure. Ceiling is capped by an inconsistent QB situation and TD-reliant deep role, but the volume supports a low-end WR2. Wk15 vs BAL is tough; wk16 vs CAR is a plus spot.

rome odunze.verdict: Breakout profile (23.6% share, 0.60 WOPR) but Burden's emergence threatens the target lead
rome odunze.report: Two years of modest scoring (145 then 146 pts, ~8.5 PPG) mask a strong underlying 2025 opportunity in 12 games (23.6% target share, 35.3% air-yards, 0.60 WOPR). The efficiency (1.74 rec EPA/g) is the concern, but improving QB play could unlock a real leap. The ceiling is a WR2 breakout; the floor is dragged down by Luther Burden competing for targets and a high 9.2 weekly stdev. Playoff slate is rough (wk15 @BUF, wk17 vs DET).

marvin harrison jr..verdict: Talent-driven bounce-back bet after a disappointing 7.5 PPG sophomore slump
marvin harrison jr..report: 2024 flashed WR2 volume (197 pts, 116 targets) before a frustrating 2025 (128 pts, 7.5 PPG, 73 targets) marred by inconsistency and a shortened 12-game advanced sample. Those advanced marks (18.1% share, 33% air-yards, 0.50 WOPR, 2.59 rec EPA/g) suggest the ability and role remain, pointing to positive regression. Ceiling is a return to WR2 territory if QB play stabilizes; floor is real given the down year and offensive uncertainty. Playoff schedule is favorable (wk15 vs NYJ, wk17 vs LV) with a late wk14 bye.

brian thomas jr..verdict: Elite 2024 rookie season makes his 2025 collapse the group's best buy-low
brian thomas jr..report: His 2024 was spectacular (284 pts, 16.7 PPG, 133 targets, 87 rec) before a stunning 2025 fall to 8.2 PPG despite retaining a 19.3% target share and 0.51 WOPR. The gutted efficiency (1.23 rec EPA/g) points to QB and scheme problems more than talent loss, giving huge rebound upside as the clear Jacksonville WR1. Ceiling is a return toward WR1 numbers; floor is genuinely low if the offense stays broken and targets keep leaking to Meyers and Hunter. The wk17 vs WSH matchup is favorable.

michael pittman jr..verdict: High-floor PPR volume man but new Pittsburgh WR2 role behind Metcalf caps upside
michael pittman jr..report: Steady target monopoly the last two years (111 targets each, 202 then 166 pts) with reliable reception volume (80 and 69 rec) gives a dependable PPR floor. Moving to Pittsburgh as the #2 behind Metcalf, however, means shared targets and a lowered ceiling. Floor is supported by his contested-catch and possession role; ceiling is limited without alpha volume in a run-leaning offense. Wk15 vs BAL is tough, wk16 vs CAR is a plus.

alec pierce.verdict: Explosive 40.6% air-yards deep threat but PUP status and TD reliance cloud the floor
alec pierce.report: Improved production in 2025 (183 pts, 10.8 PPG) driven by an extreme 40.6% air-yards share, 0.55 WOPR and a gaudy 3.72 rec EPA/g — elite big-play efficiency but volatile. As Indy's boundary deep threat his week-to-week output swings hard (8.5 stdev) and depends on connecting downfield. The PUP designation is a real availability red flag that drags the floor down significantly. Playoff slate is neutral (wk15 @TEN, wk17 @CLE).

parker washington.verdict: Breakout slot with a real 2025 leap but modest air-yards cap the ceiling
parker washington.report: Big jump from 2024 (97 pts) to 2025 (185 pts, 10.9 PPG, 95 targets, 58 rec) shows he earned a legit role in Jacksonville's offense. The 18% target share and 0.44 WOPR are solid, but the low 24.2% air-yards share means he's a short-area, volume-dependent producer. Ceiling is a WR3/flex; floor is threatened by a crowded room (Thomas, Meyers, Hunter) competing for the same throws. Wk17 vs WSH is a friendly finish.

jakobi meyers.verdict: Ultra-consistent PPR chains-mover (4.8 stdev) but touchdown-starved and now in a crowded room
jakobi meyers.report: Reliable reception volume (87, 87, 75 rec trend) and an outstanding 4.8 weekly stdev in 2025 make him one of the safest floor plays here (176 pts, 10.3 PPG). The 22.9% target share and 44 first downs confirm a steady possession role, but a paltry 0.63 rec EPA/g shows almost no big-play or scoring pop. Ceiling is limited and now compressed as a #3 option behind Thomas and Washington in Jacksonville. Playoff matchups are mixed with wk17 vs WSH the best spot.

mike evans.verdict: Age-12 vet on a new team coming off an injury-wrecked 5.0 PPG year — pure upside dart
mike evans.report: 2024 was still elite (240 pts, 14.1 PPG) but 2025 collapsed to 5.0 PPG across just 8 healthy games, a massive age-and-injury warning sign. His per-game usage when active stayed strong (24.3% share, 0.61 WOPR), so the talent flickers, but he's now 12 years in and joining San Francisco's crowded room (Pearsall, Kirk, Aiyuk). Ceiling is red-zone TD equity if healthy and featured; floor is a bust given the age, injury and target competition. Wk16 @KC is a brutal playoff draw.

carnell tate.verdict: Rookie penciled as Tennessee's WR1 — enticing role, zero proven data
carnell tate.report: No NFL data yet, but he's projected as the LWR1 in Tennessee with a clear runway ahead of Wan'Dale Robinson and an aging Calvin Ridley. The projection (211) implies strong immediate opportunity, which is the bull case for a rookie with a defined role. The floor is very low with rookie variance, questionable QB play and no track record; the ceiling is a surprise WR3 season. Playoff slate is fine (wk15 vs IND, wk17 vs PIT).

christian watson.verdict: Big-play boom-bust with a strong 0.55 WOPR but chronically low volume in a crowded room
christian watson.report: Efficiency has always been there (3.23 rec EPA/g, 20.3% share, 34.8% air-yards over 10 games in 2025) but the raw output stays low (132 then 105 pts, sub-8 PPG) because Green Bay spreads it around and he misses time. The 8.6 weekly stdev screams boom-bust. Ceiling is spike weeks as a deep threat; floor is buried by Reed, Golden and a committee approach plus recurring injury concerns. Playoff matchups are neutral (wk15 vs MIA, wk17 vs HOU).

jordyn tyson.verdict: Rookie WR2 in New Orleans with a questionable injury tag and a weak offense around him
jordyn tyson.report: No pro data and slotted as the RWR2 behind Chris Olave, meaning the target path is capped from the start. The rookie unknowns are compounded by a Questionable injury designation and a low-ceiling Saints passing attack. Ceiling is a late-season emergence if Olave misses time; floor is minimal given the depth chart and health flag. Playoff slate is average (wk16 vs ARI the best spot).

luther burden iii.verdict: Intriguing rookie efficiency but a tiny 13.1% share and 0.27 WOPR limit the current role
luther burden iii.report: His rookie line (128 pts, 7.5 PPG, 47 rec) came on very low usage — a 13.1% target share, just 10.7% air-yards and a weak 0.27 WOPR — so he's a complementary piece, not yet a target earner. The 2.00 rec EPA/g and gadget carries hint at ability worth monitoring for a year-two leap. Ceiling is a breakout if he overtakes the target hierarchy; floor is a low-volume flex sharing a room with Odunze. Playoff slate is tough (wk15 @BUF, wk17 vs DET).

matthew golden.verdict: Deep bench rookie stashed in a committee with the group's lowest usage floor
matthew golden.report: His rookie season was quiet (70 pts, 4.1 PPG) on a 12.4% target share, 19.4% air-yards and a bottom-tier 0.32 WOPR — minimal opportunity in Green Bay's crowded rotation. Listed as the RWR3, he's behind Watson and Reed with no clear path to volume. Ceiling is a distant dart-throw on year-two development; floor is roster-clogging irrelevance. Playoff matchups don't move the needle.

wan'dale robinson.verdict: Elite 30% target share and 0.65 WOPR give the safest PPR floor in this range
wan'dale robinson.report: Robinson commanded a monstrous 30.3% target share and 0.65 WOPR in 2025, seeing 140 targets in back-to-back years — that volume is the real deal for PPR floor. His 12.8 PPG jumped from 10.7 with rising efficiency (1.22 rec EPA/g), and low air-yards share caps ceiling but insulates against TD variance. Tennessee added Carnell Tate and returns Ridley/Ayomanor, so target share could dip modestly, but he remains the clear underneath focal point. A clean playoff slate (IND, @LV, PIT) and proven durability make him the top pick in this tier.

michael wilson.verdict: Broke out to 13.0 PPG with strong air-yards share behind Harrison — real leap
michael wilson.report: Wilson nearly doubled his production (7.3 to 13.0 PPG) on 126 targets with an outstanding 1.51 rec EPA/g, showing genuine growth as Arizona's clear WR2. His 31.2% air-yards share signals downfield value, though the 19.2% target share and 10.3 weekly stdev mean boom-bust weeks. Marvin Harrison sits atop the depth chart, but Wilson has carved a stable role and Bourne is no threat to it. Late bye (wk14) and neutral playoff matchups keep him a solid mid-round target with WR2 upside.

quentin johnston.verdict: Two straight 170+ point seasons at 20% target share — quietly consistent WR3
quentin johnston.report: Johnston has produced remarkably steady value, 175 then 171 points with 10+ PPG both years and a strong 0.50 WOPR plus 1.84 rec EPA/g in 2025. He operates behind Ladd McConkey but out-targets the rookie Tre' Harris, and the 28% air-yards share gives touchdown and big-play upside. The 8.4 weekly stdev reflects TD-dependence, but the floor has proven reliable. Playoff draw (SF, @MIA, KC) is middling but his role is secure enough to trust as a WR3.

khalil shakir.verdict: PPR-friendly volume and elite catch rate give a dependable floor in Buffalo
khalil shakir.report: Shakir posted 72-76 receptions in consecutive years with a 21.1% target share, and his low 8.6% air-yards share means he lives on high-percentage underneath work — great for PPR consistency (6.0 stdev). The arrival of DJ Moore threatens his target ceiling, but Josh Allen's trust and Shakir's route role keep volume intact. Ceiling is limited by the short-area profile and Buffalo's spread-the-ball offense. A back-end WR3 with one of the safer floors in this range.

josh downs.verdict: Steady slot volume with 88 targets; competent role but capped upside
josh downs.report: Downs saw 88 targets and 58 catches at an 8.0 PPG clip, down from 10.8 in 2024 as the Colts' passing game sputtered. His 17.5% target share and low 4.7 weekly stdev make him a consistent if unspectacular slot option, with Alec Pierce the field-stretcher and no real slot competition. Ceiling depends on improved QB play; floor is reliable PPR possession work. Playoff slate (@TEN, CIN, @CLE) is manageable, making him a fine depth WR with WR3 weeks.

jordan addison.verdict: 2024 form (12.5 PPG) shows the ceiling; 2025 dip and Jefferson shadow limit floor
jordan addison.report: Addison regressed hard to 7.9 PPG in 2025 after a 213-point 2024, though his 33% air-yards share and 0.50 WOPR show he still commands downfield looks as Minnesota's clear WR2. Playing second fiddle to Justin Jefferson caps target volume, and QB uncertainty adds risk. If the offense clicks he's a WR2 again; if not he's a volatile flex. The wide gap between his two seasons makes him a classic bounce-back gamble with real upside.

xavier worthy.verdict: Speed weapon in KC with 2024 upside; injury tag and target competition temper it
xavier worthy.report: Worthy managed only 6.5 PPG across 14 games in 2025 after an 11.0 PPG rookie year, and he's listed Questionable entering 2026. His 26.8% air-yards share and rushing usage (11-20 carries) give a distinctive big-play profile, but Rashee Rice's return pushes him to a clear WR2 role. The ceiling is a Mahomes-fueled explosion; the floor is a boom-bust field-stretcher with health questions. Playoff matchups (NE, SF, @LAC) are fine — upside pick with volatility.

romeo doubs.verdict: New team, strong 2025 efficiency (2.17 EPA/g), but firmly behind A.J. Brown
romeo doubs.report: Doubs improved to 9.7 PPG with an excellent 2.17 rec EPA/g and 28% air-yards share, showing he can be a productive complementary receiver. Moving to New England he projects as the clear WR2 behind A.J. Brown, with target volume dependent on Drake Maye's development. The floor is respectable given his consistent role; the ceiling requires a bigger passing pie than New England has shown. Tough playoff opener (@KC) but manageable finish — a low-risk depth add.

jayden reed.verdict: Lost 2025 to injury after strong 2024; healthy version is a flex-plus in a crowded GB room
jayden reed.report: Reed's 2025 was wiped out after just 5 games, but his 2024 (197 points, 11.6 PPG, 20 carries) plus a 2.31 rec EPA/g in limited 2025 action show real dual-threat ability. Green Bay's committee — Watson, Golden, Williams — means target share is capped even when healthy. The ceiling is a return to WR3 value with gadget usage; the floor is another lost or diluted season. High-variance bet at his ADP with genuine upside if the offense funnels his way.

makai lemon.verdict: Rookie slot in Philly with no data; talent bet behind DeVonta Smith
makai lemon.report: Lemon enters as an unproven rookie slotted as Philadelphia's WR2 behind DeVonta Smith, with Marquise Brown also in the mix. With no NFL sample, the projection (173) leans on draft capital and opportunity rather than production. The ceiling is a Year-1 breakout if he wins the slot outright; the floor is minimal usage in a run-heavy, low-volume passing attack. Purely speculative — worth a late flier for upside but no floor to lean on.

kc concepcion.verdict: Rookie in Cleveland's murky offense; upside exists but volume and QB risk loom
kc concepcion.report: Concepcion is a rookie projected as Cleveland's slot WR2 behind Jerry Jeudy, with no data to anchor expectations. Cleveland's uncertain quarterback situation and low team passing efficiency (Jeudy's -1.90 EPA in 2025 illustrates the problem) cap realistic upside. The ceiling is a rookie carving out slot volume; the floor is irrelevance in a struggling offense. A dart throw whose value hinges entirely on the QB situation improving.

chris godwin jr..verdict: Injury-shortened 2025; elite when healthy but Egbuka now leads the room
chris godwin jr..report: Godwin managed just 4.9 PPG over 9 games in 2025 as injuries derailed his season, though the 1.63 rec EPA/g shows he was still productive per snap. With Emeka Egbuka now the alpha in Tampa, Godwin projects as a WR2 whose target share and health are both question marks entering his age curve. The ceiling is a healthy return to double-digit PPG; the floor is another injury-marred, diminished year. Buy the discount cautiously.

rashid shaheed.verdict: Career-high volume in 2025 but a new SEA room behind JSN and Kupp caps him
rashid shaheed.report: Shaheed nearly doubled his 2024 output (80 to 157 points) with 92 targets and 9 carries, showing legit big-play ability, though his -0.24 rec EPA/g flags efficiency concerns. Moving into a crowded Seattle depth chart behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp likely shrinks his target share back down. The ceiling is a deep-threat flex with spike weeks; the floor is inconsistent WR4 output. Tough wk15 (@PHI) playoff opener adds risk.

travis hunter.verdict: Two-way phenom but tiny WR sample, injury flag, and negative EPA make him pure lottery ticket
travis hunter.report: Hunter's rookie WR line (3.8 PPG over 7 games, -0.33 rec EPA/g) was disappointing, complicated by his defensive duties and a Questionable tag. His 17.5% target share and low usage put him fourth in a Jacksonville room led by Brian Thomas. The ceiling is a talent-driven leap if his offensive snaps and role expand; the floor is minimal fantasy relevance while he splits two-way duties. Fascinating athlete, but the data screams caution at this price.

ricky pearsall.verdict: Elite per-snap EPA (2.97) but only 9 games and a suddenly loaded SF room
ricky pearsall.report: Pearsall flashed with a stunning 2.97 rec EPA/g and 31.8% air-yards share, but only played 9 games and produced just 5.2 PPG. The offseason additions of Mike Evans and Christian Kirk alongside Brandon Aiyuk's return crowd him out significantly — he could easily be the third or fourth option. The ceiling is real if injuries clear a path; the floor is buried on the depth chart. Difficult playoff draw (@LAC, @KC) compounds the risk.

jayden higgins.verdict: Full 17-game rookie season but modest 12.4% target share behind Nico Collins
jayden higgins.report: Higgins played all 17 games as a rookie but posted only a 12.4% target share and 0.31 WOPR, reflecting a limited role behind Nico Collins with Tank Dell returning. His 0.99 rec EPA/g was efficient on those looks, and a Year-2 leap is plausible if Dell's health falters. The ceiling is a WR3 if he consolidates targets; the floor is a low-volume WR4. Tough wk16-17 playoff finish (@PHI, @GB) limits enthusiasm.

jerry jeudy.verdict: 90-catch 2024 upside undercut by a brutal -1.90 EPA collapse in 2025
jerry jeudy.report: Jeudy's 2025 crater — 7.1 PPG and a shocking -1.90 rec EPA/g despite 106 targets — was largely a byproduct of Cleveland's disastrous QB play, not lost usage (his 20.5% target share and 35.4% air-yards share stayed strong). As the WR1 he'll get volume, but efficiency won't recover without better quarterbacking. The ceiling is a 2024-style rebound; the floor is more empty targets. High-target reclamation project with real downside risk.

jalen coker.verdict: Efficient in limited action but WR3 in Carolina with a thin target ceiling
jalen coker.report: Coker has shown per-snap efficiency (1.99 rec EPA/g) across two partial seasons but never cleared 90 points, and his 15.4% target share reflects a secondary role. Carolina's room is led by Tetairoa McMillan with Metchie and Legette competing, leaving Coker's volume uncertain. The ceiling is a modest WR4 with occasional spikes; the floor is minimal usage. Only worth a bench stash in deeper leagues.

calvin ridley.verdict: Collapsed to 2.8 PPG in 2025 and now WR3 behind rookie Tate — steep decline
calvin ridley.report: Ridley cratered from 199 points in 2024 to just 47 over 7 productive games in 2025, and Tennessee's addition of Carnell Tate plus Robinson's target dominance pushes him to third on the depth chart. His 24.4% air-yards share when active shows some residual deep value, but the trend and age (8 years exp) are alarming. The ceiling is a modest rebound if the passing game improves; the floor is fantasy irrelevance. Avoid outside deep leagues.

jalen mcmillan.verdict: 2024 flashes buried under a lost 2025 and a WR3 role behind Egbuka and Godwin
jalen mcmillan.report: McMillan showed promise in 2024 (135 points, 8.0 PPG) but managed just 30 points over 4 games in 2025, and now sits third in Tampa behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin.
