His tiny 10.8% target share and 0.26 WOPR reflect near-total marginalization. The ceiling requires injuries ahead of him to open snaps; the floor is deep-bench irrelevance. Speculative handcuff-style stash only.

tre tucker.verdict: Ascending as Vegas' clear WR1 with rising target share, WOPR and positive receiving EPA
tre tucker.report: Tucker jumped from 129 to 162 PPR points with growth in every usage marker: 19% target share, 0.47 WOPR and a strongly positive 1.28 rec EPA/g on 92 targets. As the RWR #1 ahead of Nailor, Bech and Thornton, he owns the alpha role with no serious threat, and 11 carries add cheap volume. Floor is a stable WR4 line given his 9.5 PPG; ceiling reaches WR3 territory if the offense throws more. Playoff slate is mixed (DEN, TEN, @ARI) but usage makes him the best value in this tier.

jauan jennings.verdict: Proven target earner but landed in Minnesota's crowded room behind Jefferson and Addison
jauan jennings.report: Jennings posted 211 and 173 PPR points the last two years with strong WOPR (0.48) and a healthy 19.9% target share, showing he can command volume when featured. The problem is his new home: as SWR #3 behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, his target share almost certainly compresses. Ceiling exists if injuries open a path or Minnesota leans three-wide, but the floor is a low-end flex given the target competition. His negative rec EPA in 2025 is a mild concern too.

stefon diggs.verdict: Elite 2025 production (210 pts, 4.14 rec EPA/g) but unsigned with zero projection
stefon diggs.report: Diggs bounced back to 210 PPR points on a 21.9% target share, 0.47 WOPR and a stunning 4.14 rec EPA/g — clearly still a high-end producer when healthy. The catch is he's a free agent with no team and a 0 projection, so his entire value hinges on landing spot. If he signs somewhere with volume he's a screaming value at this ADP; if he sits or takes a rotational role, the pick is dead. Age and past knee history add downside, making him a boom-or-bust dart.

deebo samuel.verdict: Versatile 188-point weapon last year but unsigned with a projection of zero
deebo samuel.report: Samuel produced 188 PPR points on 99 targets plus 17 carries, showing his dual-threat usage still travels; the 2024 season added 42 carries as a gadget piece. But like Diggs he's a free agent with no roster and no projection, so outcome is entirely landing-spot dependent. A run-heavy or three-wide scheme could restore flex value, while a marginal deal leaves him waiver fodder. The rushing role gives him a slightly safer floor than pure WRs if he signs.

cooper kupp.verdict: Declining vet buried as Seattle's SWR3 behind JSN and Shaheed
cooper kupp.report: Kupp slid from 175 to 116 PPR points as his air-yards share collapsed to 14.2% and WOPR fell to 0.34, signs of a shrinking role even before the Seattle move. Now the SWR #3 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Rashid Shaheed, the target competition is stiff and his age/injury history caps upside. His low weekly variance means a steady but unexciting floor if he plays; ceiling requires an injury ahead of him. Best treated as a late bench dart.

darnell mooney.verdict: Strong 2024 air-yards profile but tanked in 2025 amid Giants QB uncertainty
darnell mooney.report: Mooney cratered from 193 to 82 PPR points despite a still-respectable 16.2% target share and 28% air-yards share — the efficiency and touchdowns simply vanished. As the RWR #2 behind Malik Nabers he's the clear secondary option, so volume should hold, but scoring depends heavily on quarterback play. The 2024 ceiling shows what's possible if the connection clicks; the 2025 floor shows the downside. A boom-or-bust field-stretcher.

rashod bateman.verdict: Fell off a cliff to 55 points; TD-dependent behind Zay Flowers in Baltimore
rashod bateman.report: Bateman collapsed from 175 PPR points in 2024 to just 55 in 2025 as his target share dropped to 11.9% and rec EPA turned negative. His prior production was heavily touchdown-driven, and with Zay Flowers entrenched as WR1 the target ceiling is limited. There's rebound equity in a strong Ravens offense, but the floor is a non-factor if the scoring regression sticks. Tough playoff draw (@PIT, @CIN) doesn't help.

adonai mitchell.verdict: Big air-yards share but brutal efficiency (-1.01 EPA/g) on a shaky Jets offense
adonai mitchell.report: Mitchell doubled his output to 88 points in 2025 and commands real downfield volume (30.3% air-yards share, 0.44 WOPR), but his -1.01 rec EPA/g is among the worst in this group, reflecting drops and poor QB play. As LWR #2 behind Garrett Wilson he has a path to targets if the Jets throw. The ceiling case is a Year-3 efficiency leap turning that air-yards share into production; the floor is more of the same low-catch-rate frustration.

jalen nailor.verdict: Steady but capped Raiders slot behind Tucker's rising alpha role
jalen nailor.report: Nailor has posted nearly identical seasons (103 and 101 PPR points) with a modest 11.7% target share and 0.29 WOPR, plus positive rec EPA. As SWR #2 behind Tre Tucker he's a complementary piece with a defined but limited role. The floor is a low-end flex given his consistency, but the ceiling is capped unless Tucker misses time. A safe-ish but low-upside bench flyer.

ryan flournoy.verdict: Efficient breakout flashes (1.91 EPA/g) but stuck as Dallas' third option
ryan flournoy.report: Flournoy jumped from 18 to 114 PPR points with an impressive 1.91 rec EPA/g on limited volume, showing he makes the most of his chances. But as SWR #3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, his 11.1% target share leaves little room to grow unless injuries strike. The ceiling exists in a high-powered Cowboys passing game; the floor is a boom-bust flex given his 7.0 weekly stdev. A speculative upside dart.

tre' harris.verdict: Low-usage rookie year in a crowded Chargers room; upside unproven
tre' harris.report: Harris managed just 69 PPR points on a 4.1 PPG with very low weekly variance, a quiet debut. As RWR #3 behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston, his path to volume is blocked without an injury. There's developmental upside in a good offense, but nothing in the usage data yet suggests a breakout. A watch-list stash rather than a draftable flex.

jaylin noel.verdict: Minimal target share (6.0%) buried in Houston's deep receiver corps
jaylin noel.report: Noel posted 68 points but with a tiny 6.0% target share and 0.13 WOPR, meaning his production was thin and touchdown-reliant despite positive EPA. As SWR #4 behind Nico Collins, Jayden Higgins and Tank Dell, the depth chart is stacked against meaningful volume. Ceiling requires multiple injuries ahead of him; floor is waiver-wire irrelevance. Deep dynasty interest only.

jack bech.verdict: Quiet rookie campaign as a low-volume Raiders depth piece
jack bech.report: Bech scored just 42 PPR points on an 8.0% target share and 0.20 WOPR in a limited role. As LWR #3 behind Tucker and Nailor, he's a distant option in the passing game with negative rec EPA. Any fantasy relevance depends on an injury ahead of him or a Year-2 leap. A pure upside stash at this range.

isaac teslaa.verdict: Efficient on tiny volume but blocked in Detroit's top-heavy WR room
isaac teslaa.report: TeSlaa flashed a strong 1.27 rec EPA/g but on only a 5.7% target share, so his 76 points were largely touchdown-fueled. As LWR #3 behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, the target ceiling is minimal in a great offense. Volume simply isn't there without injuries, keeping him a low-floor, TD-dependent dart. Speculative only.

denzel boston.verdict: Rookie WR3 in Cleveland with no proven usage and a shaky QB situation
denzel boston.report: Boston enters as a rookie with no NFL data, slotted as the LWR #3 behind Jerry Jeudy and KC Concepcion. The 132 projection is optimistic given the depth chart and Cleveland's uncertain quarterback play. There's raw upside if he ascends the pecking order, but the floor is minimal snaps and boom-bust weeks. A pure late-round lottery ticket.

germie bernard.verdict: Rookie slot behind Metcalf and Pittman in Pittsburgh; limited near-term role
germie bernard.report: Bernard is an unproven rookie projected at 127 despite sitting as SWR #3 behind DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman. The path to targets is narrow in Year 1, making the projection aggressive. Ceiling depends on quick development or injuries ahead; floor is minimal production. A deep-league developmental hold.

antonio williams.verdict: Rookie slot in Washington with a clearer path than most in this tier
antonio williams.report: Williams comes in as the SWR #2 behind Terry McLaurin, which is a somewhat cleaner role than the other rookies here given thin competition after McLaurin. With no NFL data the 116 projection is a guess, but the depth chart offers a realistic path to slot volume. Ceiling is a surprise contributor if the targets flow; floor is a bench stash. Worth a late flyer for the opportunity.

omar cooper jr..verdict: Unknown rookie with no depth-chart clarity on the Jets
omar cooper jr..report: Cooper has no NFL data and no clear Sleeper depth-chart match, making him among the most speculative names here despite a 105 projection. Behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell on a run-oriented, QB-limited Jets offense, opportunity is uncertain. Any value is entirely projection-based upside. Deepest-league dart only.

brandon aiyuk.verdict: Injury/DNR flag and WR5 depth make him nearly undraftable despite past pedigree
brandon aiyuk.report: Aiyuk has a DNR/injury designation, a 0 projection and sits as WR5 in San Francisco behind Mike Evans, Ricky Pearsall and Christian Kirk after a lost 2025. His 2024 line (62 points) was already down amid injury. If fully healthy and re-established he has real talent, but the floor is essentially zero given the depth chart and health flags. A speculative post-injury stash at best.

chris bell.verdict: PUP rookie buried at WR5 in Miami; effectively undraftable
chris bell.report: Bell is a rookie on the PUP list slotted as LWR #5 behind Theo Wease and Malik Washington, with a health flag compounding the depth issue. The 89 projection assumes he even makes an impact, which the situation doesn't support. Floor is no meaningful role in 2026; ceiling requires health plus a major depth shakeup. Skip in redraft.

tank dell.verdict: Explosive when healthy but buried at WR3 behind Nico, Higgins and Noel after missing 2025
tank dell.report: Dell flashed 8.2 PPG on 81 targets in 2024 before a serious injury wiped out his 2025 season, and he returns to a crowded Houston room now sitting fourth in the pecking order behind Nico Collins, Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel. The ceiling is real given his big-play ability and proven target volume, but the floor is a healthy-scratch/rotational role with the depth chart stacked against him. His 'Questionable' tag and lost season make him a pure lottery ticket. Playoff slate (@PHI, @GB) is tough.

zachariah branch.verdict: Explosive rookie slot with return juice, but stuck as ATL's WR3 behind London and Dotson
zachariah branch.report: Branch enters as a dynamic rookie return man with a modest 83-point projection and no NFL production to interpret yet. Atlanta's room is topped by Drake London and Jahan Dotson, capping his target ceiling to a rotational slot role early. The upside is a gadget/return path to points if injuries open the field, but the floor is minimal snaps behind established options. Late-season schedule is reasonable (@WSH, TB, NO).

caleb douglas.verdict: Rookie with size in a thin Miami room, but no production track record to trust
caleb douglas.report: Douglas is a rookie carrying an 80-point projection with zero NFL data, currently third on Miami's depth chart behind Theo Wease and Malik Washington. Miami's WR corps is unsettled enough that a rookie could carve a role, giving him some breakout equity if he beats out the veterans. The floor is a deep-bench redshirt with a 'Questionable' injury tag already. Tough Week 17 vs BUF caps the playoff appeal.

jalen tolbert.verdict: 2024 role evaporated in 2025 (2.7 PPG, 7.6% share); new team, low priority
jalen tolbert.report: Tolbert cratered from a serviceable 8.9 PPG in 2024 to just 2.7 PPG in 2025 with a dismal 7.6% target share and 0.20 WOPR, showing his opportunity vanished. Now on Miami he sits fourth on the depth chart behind Wease, Washington and rookie Douglas, offering little path to volume. The 90-point projection looks optimistic given his usage collapse. Only a rash of injuries ahead of him unlocks any relevance.

malik washington.verdict: Ascending dual-threat slot with 106 proj and rising 14.4% share, best value in this tier
malik washington.report: Washington more than doubled his output to 6.9 PPG in 2025 while adding 17 carries, and his 14.4% target share plus 0.29 WOPR signal a growing role even if the -0.58 rec EPA/g flags inefficiency. He's now Miami's clear WR2 behind Theo Wease, and the gadget usage gives him a stable weekly floor rare for this range. The 106-point projection is the highest realistic mark in this group with modest weekly variance (3.2 stdev). Ceiling grows if the volatile Miami room opens further.

christian kirk.verdict: Faded veteran with brutal -1.92 rec EPA/g, stuck at WR3 in SF behind Evans and Pearsall
christian kirk.report: Kirk managed just 3.4 PPG in 2025 with an alarming -1.92 receiving EPA per game despite a respectable 14.6% target share, pointing to serious efficiency decline at age 30-plus. In San Francisco he's the third slot option behind Mike Evans and Ricky Pearsall with a 'Questionable' tag. The floor is deep-bench irrelevance and the ceiling requires multiple injuries ahead of him. Playoff draw (@LAC, @KC) offers no help.

savion williams.verdict: Near-zero 2025 usage (2.6% share, 0.04 WOPR); gadget flyer buried in GB
savion williams.report: Williams barely registered as a rookie with a 2.6% target share and 0.04 WOPR across 12 games, producing just 1.5 PPG. Green Bay's room is crowded with Watson, Reed and Golden ahead of him, leaving him fourth on the depth chart. His only path is expanded gadget/rush usage, but the -0.58 rush EPA/g offers little encouragement. Purely a deep-league dart throw.

chris brazzell ii.verdict: Unknown rookie with no data and no clear depth-chart role in Carolina
chris brazzell ii.report: Brazzell arrives with a 61-point projection and no NFL production or Sleeper depth-chart match, making him one of the biggest unknowns in this group. Carolina's room is led by Tetairoa McMillan with Legette and others ahead, so a defined role is unlikely early. He's a stash-only name with no reliable floor. No reason to draft outside the deepest formats.

tyreek hill.verdict: Free agent with 0 projection and a bye-week playoff slate; undraftable until signed
tyreek hill.report: Hill's 2025 ended after just four games (though those flashed a monster 0.69 WOPR and 47% air-yards share when active), and he enters 2026 as an unsigned free agent with a 0-point projection and BYE listed across all playoff weeks. Until he lands with a team, there is no usage or schedule to project and no roster to draft into. If he signs somewhere with volume, the elite pedigree could return meaningful value, but that's pure speculation. The 'Questionable' injury tag adds further risk.

de'zhaun stribling.verdict: Undrafted-caliber rookie fourth on SF's chart with no production to project
de'zhaun stribling.report: Stribling is a rookie with no NFL data sitting fourth in San Francisco behind Evans, Pearsall and Kirk. There is no target share or usage to interpret and little realistic path to snaps in a veteran room. His floor is the practice squad and his ceiling requires cascading injuries. Deep-dynasty stash only.

xavier legette.verdict: Regressed sophomore now WR4 behind McMillan; volume path narrowed sharply
xavier legette.report: Legette slipped from 7.4 PPG as a rookie to 5.3 PPG in 2025 with a -0.27 rec EPA/g, and Carolina's addition of Tetairoa McMillan pushes him to fourth on the depth chart. His 14.3% target share and 0.35 WOPR show he can still command looks if opportunity appears, but the competition ahead limits the ceiling. High weekly variance (6.5 stdev) makes him a boom-or-bust deep flyer. Playoff slate is manageable.

pat bryant.verdict: Efficient young Bronco (1.09 rec EPA/g) but stuck at WR4 in a deep room
pat bryant.report: Bryant posted a solid 1.09 rec EPA/g and 22 first downs as a rookie on limited volume (11% target share, 0.28 WOPR), hinting at real upside if opportunity expands. Denver's room is crowded, though, with Sutton, Waddle, Franklin and Mims ahead, capping his path to targets. The 73-point projection reflects that logjam. He's a watch-list stash whose ceiling hinges on injuries above him.

tory horton.verdict: Flashed big-play efficiency (1.28 rec EPA/g) as rookie but buried behind JSN, Shaheed, Kupp
tory horton.report: Horton showed juice with a 1.28 rec EPA/g and 16.9% air-yards share on limited targets, but a 6.9 weekly stdev over just 8 games underscores boom-bust volatility. Seattle's depth chart is stacked with Smith-Njigba, Shaheed and Kupp ahead, leaving him fourth in line. The ceiling is a deep-threat spike role; the floor is inconsistent snaps. Tough Week 15 at PHI.

ja'kobi lane.verdict: Intriguing rookie with 82 proj as Ravens' WR3 behind Flowers and Bateman
ja'kobi lane.report: Lane is a rookie carrying a respectable 82-point projection and lining up third in Baltimore behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman. The Ravens' pass volume is limited but their offense is efficient, giving a rookie some red-zone and downfield upside if he earns snaps. With no production history the floor is a redshirt, but the ceiling is a legitimate WR3 role by season's end. Late bye (wk13) and a tough divisional playoff slate temper enthusiasm.

ted hurst iii.verdict: No data, no depth-chart match; pure deep-league speculation in Tampa
ted hurst iii.report: Hurst has no NFL production and no Sleeper depth-chart match, making him one of the most speculative names on the board with a 65-point projection. Tampa Bay's receiving hierarchy is unclear for him, and there's no usage signal to interpret. His floor is off the roster and his ceiling is undefined. Only worth a look in the very deepest formats.

keon coleman.verdict: Best advanced profile here (0.41 WOPR, 22.8% air-yards) but DJ Moore addition caps volume
keon coleman.report: Coleman owns the strongest underlying metrics in this group — a 16.7% target share, 0.41 WOPR, 22.8% air-yards share and 26 first downs — showing genuine downfield role and 1.03 rec EPA/g efficiency. The concern is Buffalo adding DJ Moore alongside Shakir and Palmer, which drops him to a lower depth-chart spot and threatens his target share going forward. If Coleman holds his role he's a weekly flex with spike weeks; if Moore cannibalizes deep looks the floor sinks. High 6.2 stdev keeps him volatile but the ceiling is the best value at this ADP.

elijah sarratt.verdict: Undrafted-type rookie fourth in Baltimore behind Flowers, Bateman and Lane
elijah sarratt.report: Sarratt is a rookie with no data sitting fourth on Baltimore's depth chart, behind Flowers, Bateman and fellow rookie Ja'Kobi Lane. There's no usage to project and a narrow path to targets in a run-leaning offense. His floor is inactive weeks and his ceiling requires multiple injuries ahead of him. Deep-dynasty stash only.

dontayvion wicks.verdict: Efficient depth WR (1.09 rec EPA/g) but now WR4 in Philadelphia after leaving GB
dontayvion wicks.report: Wicks has posted decent efficiency (1.09 rec EPA/g in 2025, 12.8% target share, 0.31 WOPR) but his raw output slipped to 4.5 PPG amid inconsistent volume. On a new team in Philadelphia he slots fourth behind DeVonta Smith, rookie Makai Lemon and Marquise Brown, limiting the target path. The floor is deep-bench and the ceiling needs injuries ahead of him. High 6.4 stdev makes him a touchdown-dependent dart.

kayshon boutte.verdict: Broke out with 2.63 rec EPA/g and 27 first downs, but A.J. Brown's arrival crushes his role
kayshon boutte.report: Boutte quietly posted an excellent 2.63 rec EPA/g with a 21.5% air-yards share and 27 first downs in 2025, showing he can produce with big-play efficiency. The problem is New England importing A.J. Brown, which shoves Boutte to WR3 and slashes his projected target volume for 2026. If Brown or Doubs miss time his ceiling is a genuine WR3/flex; the floor is a rotational deep threat. High 7.3 weekly stdev signals boom-bust weeks and a tough Week 15 at KC.

nick westbrook-ikhine.verdict: Collapsed from 136 pts to 20 as role vanished (5.2% share); 96 proj looks aspirational
nick westbrook-ikhine.report: NWI's production cratered from 136 points in 2024 to just 20 in 2025 as his target share collapsed to 5.2% and WOPR to 0.11, a stark usage warning. Now in Indianapolis he sits third behind Alec Pierce and Josh Downs, and the 96-point projection seems to bank on a role he no longer commands. The floor is deep-bench irrelevance; only red-zone volume could salvage TD-dependent value. The 2024 season was heavily touchdown-fueled, making the projection optimistic.

darius slayton.verdict: Big-play WR3 with real air-yards share; TD-dependent boom-bust flier only
darius slayton.report: Slayton's 25% air-yards share and 0.41 WOPR show genuine downfield usage even as the Giants' #3, and his 1.29 rec EPA/g is the best receiving efficiency in this group. The ceiling is a multi-TD deep-ball spike week, but the floor is grim given only a 15.5% target share behind Nabers and Mooney and just 5.8 PPG. He's a bench dart throw whose value hinges on big plays, and the wk16 @DET / wk17 @DAL playoff slate offers no relief. Draft only as depth in deep leagues.

andrei iosivas.verdict: Efficient CIN slot buried behind Chase/Higgins; injury to a starter unlocks flex value
andrei iosivas.report: Iosivas posted a positive 0.78 rec EPA/g and 24 first downs, showing he's productive on limited volume, and his 2024 120-point season proves upside exists when targets flow. The problem is the depth chart: he's the third option behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, capping his 10.2% target share. His floor is near-zero relevance if both starters stay healthy, but his ceiling as a contingency in Cincinnati's high-volume passing attack is real, and the wk17 BAL matchup could pay off in a shootout. Best profile of this tier as a stash.

dyami brown.verdict: Low-usage WSH WR3 with negative efficiency; deep-league dart at best
dyami brown.report: Brown's 9.9% target share and negative -0.19 rec EPA/g are red flags, and his production actually declined from 2024 (4.0 PPG) to 2025 (2.9 PPG). Buried behind McLaurin and Antonio Williams, there's no clear path to volume, and the 0.27 WOPR confirms limited opportunity. The ceiling requires multiple injuries ahead of him plus positive game script, while the floor is total irrelevance. The 2026 projection of 85 looks generous relative to his usage trend.

jahan dotson.verdict: Worst efficiency in group; ATL WR2 in name only behind London
jahan dotson.report: Dotson's -1.00 rec EPA/g is alarming, and his 8.3% target share with just 10 first downs shows he barely moves the needle despite the #2 depth-chart label. In Atlanta's run-leaning, low-volume passing attack he competes with Drake London for scraps and rising Zachariah Branch. The ceiling assumes a role expansion that the data gives no reason to expect, and the floor is waiver-wire irrelevance. Only a late-round name-value flier hoping for a change of scenery or scheme shift.

trey mcbride.verdict: The clear TE1 — target hog with 27.9% share and elite WOPR, floor and ceiling both league-best at the position.
trey mcbride.report: McBride jumped from 14.7 to 18.6 PPG in 2025 while commanding a massive 27.9% target share, 24.6% air-yards share and 0.59 WOPR — this is genuine volume, not TD luck, backed by 4.28 rec EPA/g and 63 first downs. He has zero TE competition in Arizona (Higgins/Quitoriano are afterthoughts), so 160+ targets is repeatable. Floor case is a near-100-target guarantee even if Arizona's offense stalls; ceiling is another top-overall-TE finish. Playoff slate (NYJ, @NO, LV) is soft. He's the safest premium TE pick.

brock bowers.verdict: Elite talent with a monster 2024 rookie line; 2025 dip was injury/QB-driven, huge rebound ceiling.
brock bowers.report: Bowers exploded for 15.5 PPG as a rookie (153 targets), then fell to 10.4 PPG in an injury-shortened 12-game 2025, but his underlying 23.4% target share and 0.53 WOPR stayed strong. The drop was more about missed time and Vegas's shaky passing game than skill decline. Ceiling is a return to elite TE1 form; floor reflects injury recurrence and offensive-environment risk plus higher weekly variance (stdev 10.5). Mayer exists but Bowers is unquestioned WR-caliber alpha. Worth the early pick on talent alone.

colston loveland.verdict: Ascending young Bear with strong rookie EPA; year-two leap potential as Kmet fades.
colston loveland.report: Loveland posted 9.7 PPG and a 2.97 rec EPA/g as a rookie despite a modest 16.6% target share, signaling efficiency ahead of volume. Kmet remains the #2 but the trend points to Loveland absorbing more of Chicago's passing tree in year two. Ceiling is a top-6 TE breakout if the target share climbs toward 20%; floor is a still-usable low-end starter given weekly variance. Playoff schedule (@BUF, GB, DET) is only average. Draft the growth curve.

tyler warren.verdict: Ultra-consistent rookie (stdev 4.7) with 112 targets; the safest floor of the young TEs.
tyler warren.report: Warren logged all 17 games with a remarkably low 4.7 weekly stdev, drawing 112 targets and a 21.5% share as a rookie — that's a stable, high-floor role. The advanced efficiency (0.93 rec EPA/g, low air-yards share) shows a short-area chain-mover rather than a big-play threat, capping the true ceiling somewhat. No meaningful TE competition in Indy means the volume is locked in. Playoff slate (@TEN, CIN, @CLE) is fine. Reliable weekly starter with room to grow.

kyle pitts sr..verdict: Finally delivered 12.4 PPG on 118 targets in 2025; volume rebound makes him a viable mid-round starter.
kyle pitts sr..report: Pitts nearly doubled his output from 2024 (7.7) to 2025 (12.4 PPG) on a healthy 118 targets and 88 catches, suggesting the long-awaited role finally materialized. Weekly variance is high (stdev 9.6), so boom-bust risk remains, and his career has been maddeningly inconsistent. Ceiling is a top-5 TE season if the target volume holds; floor is another frustrating quiet stretch. Soft playoff draw (@WSH, TB, NO) is a bonus. Reasonable value at TE.

harold fannin jr..verdict: Rookie produced 21.8% target share and 107 targets; real volume in Cleveland's thin passing game.
harold fannin jr..report: Fannin earned a surprising 107 targets and 21.8% share as a rookie, posting a steady 6.0 stdev — that's meaningful, repeatable opportunity even if his 0.09 rec EPA/g flags weak efficiency in a poor offense. The ceiling depends on QB play improving; the floor is respectable because the target volume alone sustains fantasy relevance. No real TE competition ahead of him. Playoff schedule is neutral (@NYG, @BAL, IND). A solid late-round starter bet.

sam laporta.verdict: Injury-shortened 2025 (9g) masks strong 4.05 EPA efficiency; healthy rebound in elite offense possible.
sam laporta.report: LaPorta cratered to 6.3 PPG across just 9 games in 2025 after 10.3 in 2024, but his 4.05 rec EPA/g and 18.5% share when active show the talent is intact — this was availability, not decline. In Detroit's high-powered offense a healthy season could return top-8 TE value. Floor is scary given the missed time and target competition from a run-heavy attack; ceiling is a full rebound to double-digit PPG. Value is depressed by the down year — buy the discount.

george kittle.verdict: Elite when healthy (4.21 EPA/g) but PUP tag and age 32+ raise real availability red flags.
george kittle.report: Kittle remains hyper-efficient — 21.5% share, 4.21 rec EPA/g over 11 games in 2025 — and topped 13.9 PPG in a full 2024. The concern is the PUP designation entering 2026 plus mounting age, which drags the floor considerably. Ceiling is still a top-5 TE if he plays 15+ games; floor is a wasted pick if the injury lingers. Tough playoff draw (@LAC, @KC, PHI) adds risk. Elite ceiling, but discount heavily for health.

dallas goedert.verdict: Bounced back to 10.9 PPG in 2025; steady red-zone role in Philly makes him a safe streamer-plus.
dallas goedert.report: Goedert rebounded from a dismal 2024 (6.1) to 10.9 PPG in 2025 on 82 targets and a healthy 20.8% share with solid 2.41 rec EPA/g. In Philadelphia's run-leaning but efficient offense his role is stable, though the target ceiling is capped by the Hurts-to-WR pecking order. Floor is decent given the target share; ceiling is a low-end TE1. Playoff slate is mixed (SEA, HOU, @SF). Dependable but unspectacular.

travis kelce.verdict: Still a 108-target chain-mover at 20% share, but age-driven decline caps upside; safe floor.
travis kelce.report: Kelce held remarkably steady at 11.4 PPG on 108 targets and a 20% share in 2025, and his 46 first downs show he's still central to KC's offense. At 13 years of experience the trajectory only points down, limiting the ceiling to a middling TE1. The floor is one of the safest at the position because the volume and QB are elite. Playoff draw (NE, SF, @LAC) is average. Draft for reliability, not upside.

jake ferguson.verdict: 102 targets but tiny 8.9% air-yards share — high-volume dink role with a capped ceiling.
jake ferguson.report: Ferguson leapt to 11.1 PPG on 102 targets in 2025, a huge bump from 2024, but the 8.9% air-yards share and 0.31 WOPR reveal an extremely shallow, low-value target profile. The PPR volume gives him a decent floor; the lack of downfield or red-zone usage limits the ceiling. No TE competition in Dallas keeps the targets flowing. Playoff slate is fine (@LAR, JAX, NYG). A volume-driven, TD-light starter.

mark andrews.verdict: Sharp decline to 7.7 PPG in 2025 with near-zero EPA; aging and target-share erosion are concerning.
mark andrews.report: Andrews fell from 11.1 to 7.7 PPG in 2025 as his target share slid to 17.1% and his rec EPA cratered to 0.09 — the efficiency that once carried him has vanished. He remains TD-dependent (10 carries hint at goal-line usage) but Baltimore's spread-out passing game no longer funnels through him. Floor is a bust; ceiling is a modest TD-fueled rebound. Tough divisional playoff draw (@PIT, CLE, @CIN). Fading asset.

tucker kraft.verdict: Elite efficiency (4.89 EPA/g) but PUP tag and Green Bay's crowded targets create big variance.
tucker kraft.report: Kraft flashed elite per-game efficiency (4.89 rec EPA/g) over 8 games in 2025 before injury, and his 9.6 PPG in 2024 shows a solid baseline. The PUP designation and Green Bay's committee passing attack (low 9.6% air-yards share) cloud the outlook. Ceiling is a breakout if healthy and targets consolidate; floor is grim given the injury and Musgrave competition. High-variance late-round dart throw.

t.j. hockenson.verdict: Low-ceiling possession TE (10.2% air-yards) with a stable but uninspiring 6.6 PPG floor.
t.j. hockenson.report: Hockenson's 6.6 PPG in 2025 came with a very low 4.4 stdev — consistent, but consistently mediocre, on a 15.9% share and paltry 10.2% air-yards share. Minnesota's offense and QB uncertainty cap his upside, and Josh Oliver siphons some snaps. Floor is safe for a bye-week fill-in; ceiling is a fringe TE1 only if volume spikes. Playoff slate is neutral. A boring, low-variance depth piece.

kenyon sadiq.verdict: Rookie with a Questionable tag and Mason Taylor competition — pure speculation, no proven role.
kenyon sadiq.report: Sadiq has no NFL data and enters as the nominal Jets TE1 but faces Mason Taylor for snaps and carries a Questionable injury flag. The projection of 162 is optimistic for an unproven rookie in a weak offense. Ceiling requires him seizing the job outright and the passing game supporting a TE; floor is irrelevance. Strictly a late-round upside stash. Too many unknowns to trust as a starter.

isaiah likely.verdict: New team (NYG) offers a shot at real volume after a wasted 2025 behind Andrews; upside bet.
isaiah likely.report: Likely collapsed to 3.6 PPG in 2025 stuck behind Andrews (12% share), but his 2024 (7.3 PPG on 58 targets) shows what he can do with opportunity. A move to the Giants makes him the clear TE1, and a wide-open target tree could unlock a career year. Floor is low given QB uncertainty and unproven volume in the new offense; ceiling is a mid-range TE1 if he earns 90+ targets. Speculative but intriguing at his ADP.

dalton kincaid.verdict: Efficient (3.28 EPA/g) but Buffalo's spread offense and 14.9% share cap consistent production.
dalton kincaid.report: Kincaid ticked up to 7.4 PPG in 2025 with strong 3.28 rec EPA/g and a healthy 20.7% air-yards share, hinting at downfield upside. The problem is Buffalo's ultra-distributed passing game keeps his target share (14.9%) and total volume low. Ceiling is a low-end TE1 in a great offense; floor is a boom-bust flex. Playoff draw is manageable (CHI, @DEN, @MIA). A talent-vs-volume bet.

hunter henry.verdict: Reliable 10.5 PPG on 87 targets and 42 first downs — a boring but genuinely usable NE starter.
hunter henry.report: Henry quietly posted 10.5 PPG on 87 targets with 42 first downs in 2025, a solid uptick from 2024, and at age/experience 10 he remains New England's steady TE1. The 17.4% share and 2.22 EPA/g are unremarkable but stable, giving him a dependable weekly floor. Ceiling is limited by his age and the offense's ceiling; tough playoff slate (@KC, @NYJ, DEN) hurts. A safe, low-upside bye-week plug.

terrance ferguson.verdict: Buried rookie (6.5% share) behind Parkinson and Higbee — no path to relevance yet.
terrance ferguson.report: Ferguson managed just 3.1 PPG on a tiny 6.5% target share and 0.18 WOPR as a rookie, and the Rams' crowded TE room (Parkinson, Higbee, Allen) offers no clear opening. The projection of 136 assumes a major role change that isn't evident in the data. Ceiling requires him leapfrogging the depth chart; floor is waiver-wire irrelevance. Deep-league dynasty stash only.

juwan johnson.verdict: Sneaky-steady 10.6 PPG on 102 targets in 2025; undervalued volume in New Orleans.
juwan johnson.report: Johnson posted a quietly productive 10.6 PPG on 102 targets and a 4.7 stdev in 2025, with a solid 17.7% share and 41 first downs — genuinely usable output in a thin NO passing game. The addition of Noah Fant is a mild threat, and the offense's overall weakness caps the ceiling. Floor is decent given the established volume; ceiling is a low-end TE1 if the targets hold. Good value at his ADP for a stable streaming option.

dalton schultz.verdict: Best real usage in this tier: 106 targets, 19.1% share, 0.39 WOPR make him a stable TE1
dalton schultz.report: Schultz's 2025 leap to 178 PPR points on a 19.1% target share and 0.39 WOPR is the most legit workload of any TE in this range, and his 2.16 rec EPA/g shows it wasn't TD luck. His 5.5 weekly stdev is low for the position, giving a dependable weekly floor with matchup-proof volume as Houston's clear TE1. Downside is a return toward his 2024 output (118 pts, 7.0 ppg) if the offense concentrates elsewhere, but the target trend points up. Playoff slate is mixed — @PHI wk16 and @GB wk17 are tough, but he's a target hog who plays through it.

brenton strange.verdict: Ascending young TE1 with a 0.32 WOPR and rising target share — best upside bet in the mid-tier
brenton strange.report: Strange jumped from 91 to 118 points with a healthy 15.6% target share and 0.32 WOPR in only 12 charted games, and his 2.61 rec EPA/g leads this cluster — real, efficient usage trending forward. As an entrenched TE1 entering year three with no meaningful target competition on the depth chart, he's a clean breakout candidate at ADP. Floor is limited by a still-modest 6.9 ppg and a run-heavy Jacksonville script. Playoff draw (@HOU, @DAL, WSH) is neutral.

chig okonkwo.verdict: Consistency play: lowest variance in the tier with a real 79-target role, now the WSH TE1
chig okonkwo.report: Okonkwo has posted back-to-back stable seasons (114 then 124 pts) with the lowest weekly stdev (4.3) among these TEs, making him a plug-and-play floor option. His 15.0% target share and 79 targets are solid, though a tiny 8.7% air-yards share caps big-play upside. Moving into a new offense adds uncertainty about his role, but as the clear TE1 he should retain volume. The consistency profile is worth more than his ADP suggests.

pat freiermuth.verdict: Bought the 2024 name, but 2025 collapse (168→114 pts, WOPR 0.26) flags real decline
pat freiermuth.report: Freiermuth fell from a career-best 168 points in 2024 to 114 in 2025 as his target share cratered to 11.3% and WOPR dropped to 0.26 — a worrying forward signal in a Pittsburgh offense with crowded target competition. He remains the clear TE1, so a partial rebound toward his 2024 volume is the ceiling case, but the 2025 usage says the floor is closer to a low-end streamer. His 1.55 rec EPA/g is uninspiring. Playoff schedule (BAL, CAR, @TEN) is a plus with two soft matchups.

aj barner.verdict: Scored 147 but on only 7.7% air-yards share — heavily TD-dependent, expect regression
aj barner.report: Barner's 147-point breakout is inflated: a 13.8% target share and paltry 7.7% air-yards share mean he lived on red-zone looks and rushing carries (10 rush att), a profile that regresses hard. His 35 first downs and role diversity (rush EPA/g 0.43) are encouraging, but the underlying receiving usage is that of a low-end TE1/streamer. Rookie Elijah Arroyo lurks as target competition in Seattle. The ceiling requires him to repeat the TD rate, which is unlikely.

oronde gadsden.verdict: Big-play rookie ceiling but 7.4 stdev and Njoku competition make him boom-bust
oronde gadsden.report: Gadsden flashed as a rookie with 131 points but a huge 7.4 weekly stdev signals a spike-week, feast-or-famine profile. The addition of David Njoku as the #2 (and arguably a threat to touches) muddies the target picture despite Gadsden holding the TE1 label. Ceiling is real if he consolidates the role and the passing game leans on him, but the floor is low given inconsistency and shared work. Playoff slate (SF, @MIA, KC) is a mixed bag.

evan engram.verdict: New Denver role gives a decent 13.7% share and 0.31 WOPR, but low ceiling at this age
evan engram.report: Engram's move to Denver produced a steady 103 points on a 13.7% target share and 0.31 WOPR with a low 4.0 stdev — a safe but capped profile in year nine. He gets volume as the clear TE1, but 0.22 rec EPA/g shows the efficiency has faded and the ceiling is modest. Floor is respectable for a streamer given the reliable target share. Playoff draw is fine (@LV, BUF, @NE).

cade otton.verdict: Solid 17.4% target share but 0.21 rec EPA/g and volatility make him a matchup streamer
cade otton.report: Otton owns a healthy 17.4% target share and 0.34 WOPR, so the volume is real, but his 0.21 rec EPA/g and dip from 141 to 122 points show declining efficiency. He's the unquestioned Tampa TE1 with no depth-chart threat, giving a stable target floor. High weekly variance (6.0 stdev) and TD dependence cap the appeal. Playoff schedule (NO, @ATL, LAR) is neutral-to-good.

gunnar helm.verdict: Rookie with a locked TE1 role but tiny 10.7% share and 0.24 EPA/g — year-two dart throw
gunnar helm.report: Helm turned in a quiet rookie year (92 pts, 5.4 ppg) with a low 10.7% target share, 8.0% air-yards share and near-zero 0.24 rec EPA/g — usage that says he wasn't yet a focal point. He is the clear Tennessee TE1 with minimal competition, so a second-year bump is plausible if the offense develops. The ceiling is speculative and the floor is bench-level. Playoff draw (IND, @LV, PIT) is fine.

greg dulcich.verdict: Efficient when on the field (1.95 EPA/g) but injury history and only 10 games cap trust
greg dulcich.report: Dulcich showed real efficiency in Miami with a 15.4% target share, 0.30 WOPR and strong 1.95 rec EPA/g, but he played just 10 games — a recurring availability problem. If healthy and cemented as TE1 he has streamer-plus upside, but the games-missed risk drags the floor way down. The Miami passing volume gives a reasonable ceiling in the right stretch. Wk17 vs BUF is a tougher spot.

mike gesicki.verdict: Fell off a cliff (142→71 pts) with 10.3% share behind Erick All — avoid
mike gesicki.report: Gesicki's collapse from 142 to 71 points as his target share fell to 10.3% is a stark decline signal, with Erick All returning to eat into the Cincinnati TE role. The 13.1% air-yards share hints at occasional downfield value, but 4.2 ppg is barely rosterable. Ceiling requires an injury ahead of him or a target-share rebound that the trend doesn't support. Floor is off your bench entirely.

david njoku.verdict: Now a TE2 behind Gadsden in LAC after a lost 2025 — negative EPA and shrinking role
david njoku.report: Njoku cratered from 149 points in 2024 to 86 in 2025 with a negative -0.33 rec EPA/g over just 11 games, and his move to the Chargers lands him behind Oronde Gadsden on the depth chart. As the listed TE2 in a split, his path to fantasy relevance requires an injury or a role reversal. The ceiling exists only on talent and past pedigree, not current usage. This is a late dart with a bench-level floor.

michael mayer.verdict: Talented but buried behind Brock Bowers — pure Bowers handcuff with no standalone value
michael mayer.report: Mayer improved to 74 points but his -0.76 rec EPA/g and clear position behind Brock Bowers on the depth chart cap him at deep-league handcuff status. His 13.7% share came in relief work; with a healthy Bowers there simply aren't enough targets. Standalone value is minimal and the floor is a waiver-wire afterthought. Only draftable as insurance for a Bowers manager.

jake tonges.verdict: Kittle backup with a bottom-tier 33 projection — irrelevant unless Kittle misses time
jake tonges.report: Tonges posted 93 points filling in during 2025, but he sits firmly behind George Kittle and carries a rock-bottom 33-point projection reflecting expected garbage-time-only usage. His 1.42 rec EPA/g when on the field is fine, but there are no targets to be had behind a healthy Kittle. This is strictly a Kittle-injury handcuff with essentially no standalone floor. Not worth a redraft pick.

josh allen.verdict: Every-down dual-threat with the safest elite ceiling in the position — reliable 21-22 PPG floor.
josh allen.report: Allen has posted 22.3 and 21.4 PPG the last two seasons on 100+ carries per year, giving him a rushing floor no other QB matches on volume plus efficiency (rush EPA/g 2.42). His pass EPA/g 4.46 and positive CPOE confirm the production is real, not TD-luck. Floor case is a top-3 finish; ceiling is the overall QB1. Playoff slate (CHI, @DEN, @MIA) is fine and he has no roster threat.

jayden daniels.verdict: 2024 monster (20.9 PPG, 148 carries) whose 2025 was wrecked by injury — buy the healthy rushing ceiling.
jayden daniels.report: In a full 2024 he ran 148 times and scored 356 points as a top-tier fantasy QB, but 2025 was a lost year (7 games, negative pass EPA and CPOE) that tanked his ADP. Interpreting forward, the rushing volume is the elite differentiator if health returns. Ceiling is a top-3 season; floor is another injury-shortened dud given the running style. No depth-chart threat with Mariota behind him.

lamar jackson.verdict: 430-point ceiling in 2024, injury-shortened 2025 — the single highest QB upside if he plays 17.
lamar jackson.report: Jackson's 2024 (25.3 PPG, absurd 6.0 stdev) is the best fantasy QB season on this board, and even 2025's down/injury year showed strong efficiency (pass EPA 1.40, rush EPA 1.59, +2.9 CPOE). The dual-threat volume gives him league-winning weekly upside. Floor is missed games plus TD variance dragging him toward QB10; ceiling is the overall QB1. Division playoff slate (@PIT, CLE, @CIN) is tough but he's beaten them.

drake maye.verdict: Genuine 2025 breakout — elite 9.72 pass EPA/g and +12.2 CPOE with 103 carries and a 5.2 stdev.
drake maye.report: Maye jumped from 10.4 to 20.7 PPG with the most convincing efficiency profile in this range: 9.72 pass EPA/g, +12.2 CPOE and a remarkably low 5.2 weekly stdev signal a stable, high floor. He added a rushing element (103 carries) that raises the ceiling toward top-5. Floor case is efficiency regression to the mean; ceiling is a top-3 QB. The playoff draw (@KC, @NYJ, DEN) is a genuine negative.

jalen hurts.verdict: Rushing-TD floor keeps him a rock-solid QB1 even as passing volume stays modest.
jalen hurts.report: Hurts banked 17.6 and 18.5 PPG on the strength of goal-line carries (105-150 rushes) with solid efficiency (pass EPA 2.14, +4.2 CPOE). That designed-run role gives him one of the safest weekly floors, though the ceiling is capped versus the pure-volume passers. Floor is a low-end QB1; ceiling is top-5 if TD variance breaks right. Great home-heavy playoff slate (SEA, HOU) with only @SF a concern.

joe burrow.verdict: Elite when upright (21.9 PPG in 2024) but 2025 was another injury wipeout — pure boom-bust.
joe burrow.report: Burrow's 2024 (373 points) and his 2025 per-game efficiency (4.58 pass EPA, +4.6 CPOE) show a top-5 passer whenever healthy, but he managed only 8 games last year. No rushing floor means his value is entirely tied to the arm and to health. Ceiling is the overall passing QB1; floor is another lost season. Soft playoff run (@CAR, @IND) is a bonus if he's playing.

jaxson dart.verdict: Second-year rushing threat (86 carries, 2.72 rush EPA/g) with real dual-threat upside but shaky passing.
jaxson dart.report: Dart flashed as a runner in his first year (86 carries, elite 2.72 rush EPA/g) which underpins a fantasy-friendly floor, but the passing (0.24 EPA/g, -0.6 CPOE, 11.1 stdev) is volatile and unproven. Forward view: the legs make him a streamer-plus with QB1 spike weeks. Ceiling is a Daniels-lite dual-threat breakout; floor is inconsistency and a benching risk with Winston behind him. Playoff schedule is middling.

trevor lawrence.verdict: Bounced back to 19.9 PPG with added rushing (82 carries) — a reliable low-end QB1.
trevor lawrence.report: Lawrence rebounded hard from 8.5 to 19.9 PPG in 2025 while adding rushing volume (82 carries, 1.52 rush EPA/g) that lifts his floor. The passing efficiency was only okay (2.26 EPA/g, -1.3 CPOE), so the ceiling is more QB8-10 than top-5. Floor is another mediocre pocket season if the run element fades. No roster threat; playoff slate (@HOU, @DAL, WSH) is neutral.

dak prescott.verdict: Efficient 18.5 PPG when healthy (6.66 pass EPA/g) but injury 'Questionable' tag caps confidence.
dak prescott.report: Prescott returned to form in 2025 (18.5 PPG, strong 6.66 pass EPA/g) after an injury-ruined 2024, and the low 8.0 stdev points to weekly reliability. The negative rush EPA means he's a pure pocket passer, so volume in a pass-heavy Dallas offense is the driver. Ceiling is a top-6 passing season; floor is another injury derailment given his tag. Playoff slate is manageable (JAX, NYG at home).

bo nix.verdict: Steady two-year producer (~18 PPG) with useful legs and a low weekly stdev.
bo nix.report: Nix has quietly logged 18.7 and 17.9 PPG across two full seasons with 80+ carries each year, and the consistency (8.1 stdev) makes him a dependable back-end QB1. Efficiency is fine but unspectacular (3.72 pass EPA/g, slightly negative CPOE), which caps the ceiling. Floor is solid; ceiling is roughly QB8. The 'Questionable' tag and a tough wk16 vs BUF are minor dings.

brock purdy.verdict: Elite efficiency (7.01 EPA/g, +7.7 CPOE) buried under a 9-game injury year — high-upside bounce-back.
brock purdy.report: When healthy in 2025 Purdy posted outstanding metrics (7.01 pass EPA/g, +7.7 CPOE, 1.80 rush EPA/g), but he played only 9 games and his 12.1 stdev screams boom-bust. In a healthy SF offense the ceiling is a top-6 passer; the floor is another injury-shortened season with wild weekly swings. No depth threat. Playoff slate (@LAC, @KC, PHI) is difficult.

matthew stafford.verdict: Posted 20.6 PPG with elite 8.85 pass EPA/g in 2025 — but age and zero rushing cap the profile.
matthew stafford.report: Stafford's 2025 was excellent (350 points, 20.6 PPG, 8.85 pass EPA/g, 6.8 stdev), a stark rebound from 2024's 12.6 PPG. Forward-looking, the arm-only volume in a strong Rams offense supports another QB1 finish, but at 17 years experience decline and injury are real threats. Ceiling is top-6; floor is age catching up quickly. Neutral playoff slate.

caleb williams.verdict: Improved to 18.7 PPG with rushing volume, but -3.4 CPOE flags TD-driven, unstable production.
caleb williams.report: Williams took a step up to 18.7 PPG in 2025 with 77 carries adding a floor, yet the -3.4 CPOE and modest 2.48 pass EPA/g suggest the fantasy output ran ahead of the underlying passing. Forward view: further development could unlock a top-8 ceiling, but the accuracy metrics warn of regression. Floor is streamer territory; ceiling is low-end QB1. Rough wk15 at BUF in the playoffs.

justin herbert.verdict: Metronome-steady ~17 PPG two years running — safe but low-ceiling with weak passing EPA.
justin herbert.report: Herbert has produced back-to-back ~16.8 PPG seasons with excellent consistency (6.0 stdev in 2024), and 83 carries in 2025 quietly help. The efficiency is modest (1.01 pass EPA/g), so he profiles as a floor-based QB2 rather than a spike-week QB1. Ceiling is capped around QB10; floor is a very playable streamer. Playoff slate (SF, @MIA, KC) is a mixed bag.

patrick mahomes.verdict: Name-brand but two straight ~16.8 PPG floors and a 'Questionable' tag temper the ceiling.
patrick mahomes.report: Mahomes has settled into 16.6-16.8 PPG the last two years with rising rushing volume (64 carries) and strong per-game passing EPA (4.87), but only 14 games in 2025 and a Questionable tag add risk. The ceiling remains a top-5 passer if the receiving corps improves; the floor is another mid-pack, TD-variance-driven year. Justin Fields lurking is a non-factor unless injured. Home playoff games help.

kyler murray.verdict: New team, McCarthy competition and a disastrous 2025 — dart throw on 2024's rushing upside.
kyler murray.report: Murray cratered in 2025 (4.6 PPG over 5 games) and now lands in Minnesota behind a competitive J.J. McCarthy, making even a starting role uncertain. His 2024 (17.5 PPG, 78 carries) shows the dual-threat ceiling still exists if he wins the job. Floor is a bench/backup non-factor; ceiling is a mid-range QB1 in a good offense. Pure late-round upside stash.

tyler shough.verdict: Low-floor NO passer with poor efficiency (-2.7 CPOE) and a Rattler timeshare threat.
tyler shough.report: Shough managed just 9.3 PPG with weak underlying numbers (0.19 pass EPA/g, -2.7 CPOE) and virtually no rushing floor, in a bottom-tier Saints offense. Forward-looking there's little to project up other than natural development and cheap price. Floor is a benching behind Rattler; ceiling is low-end streamer weeks. Only for deep two-QB formats.

daniel jones.verdict: Surprisingly strong 2025 efficiency (5.02 EPA/g) in Indy — a sneaky late-round streamer.
daniel jones.report: Jones posted a career-best profile in 2025 (13.3 PPG, 5.02 pass EPA/g, +2.6 CPOE, 1.24 rush EPA/g) that suggests the Colts scheme fits him. The rushing adds a modest floor, and if the volume holds he's a usable QB2. Floor is inconsistency and TD dependence; ceiling is a fringe QB1 in a good offense. Riley Leonard behind him is a lurking threat but not immediate.

jared goff.verdict: Efficient pocket passer (6.26 EPA/g) in an elite offense but zero rushing keeps him a streamer.
jared goff.report: Goff put up 17.5 PPG with strong efficiency (6.26 pass EPA/g, +2.9 CPOE) behind Detroit's high-powered offense, and 2024's 19.1 PPG shows the ceiling. The complete lack of rushing (19 carries) means he needs volume and TDs, so weekly variance runs high. Floor is a low-end QB2; ceiling is a matchup-based QB1. Playoff slate (@MIN, @CHI on the road) is division-heavy.

baker mayfield.verdict: Fell from 21.5 to 16.0 PPG with poor 2025 efficiency (0.04 EPA/g) — regression looks real.
baker mayfield.report: Mayfield's 2024 (21.5 PPG, 366 points) was a career outlier, and 2025 regressed hard to 16.0 PPG with essentially neutral passing (0.04 pass EPA/g, -2.5 CPOE); his rushing (2.10 rush EPA/g) is the lone bright spot. Forward view leans toward the modest 2025 baseline over the 2024 spike. Floor is a low QB2; ceiling is a matchup streamer with occasional spike weeks. Late-round only.

malik willis.verdict: Projection assumes a starting job that isn't secured; career backup with rushing flashes
malik willis.report: Willis has been a pure backup the last two seasons (3.0 PPG, ~20 carries), and his 2025 advanced marks come from just 4 games as a passer — a tiny, noisy sample. The 238 projection bakes in a full-time MIA role that competition from Quinn Ewers and Cam Miller makes uncertain. Ceiling exists via mobility and a real starter workload, but the floor is a clipboard. Playoff slate (@GB, LAC, BUF) is neutral-to-tough if he even holds the job.

jordan love.verdict: Best of this streaming tier — stable dual-year floor, strong pass EPA, rushing upside
jordan love.report: Love has posted an identical 13.8 PPG in back-to-back seasons with the best pass EPA/g (7.37) and healthy rush EPA (0.82) in this group, giving him the most trustworthy weekly floor here. He's the entrenched GB starter with only Tyrod Taylor behind him, so job security is a non-issue. Ceiling is a top-10 finish if the passing volume ticks up; floor is a low-end QB2. The playoff draw (MIA, @CHI, HOU) is favorable enough to stream in December.

cam ward.verdict: Year-2 leap bet, but 2025 pass EPA was ugly (-6.42) on a thin TEN roster
cam ward.report: Ward's rookie year produced 11.0 PPG with low weekly variance but a dreadful -6.42 pass EPA/g, signaling volume without efficiency. His 39 carries add a modest rushing floor and there's clear developmental upside as the unquestioned starter. Floor is capped by a weak supporting cast; ceiling depends on a real sophomore jump. Playoff schedule (IND, @LV, PIT) is manageable.

c.j. stroud.verdict: Bounce-back candidate with elite-arm pedigree and rising rush EPA — buy the dip
c.j. stroud.report: Stroud's counting stats slid to 12.3 PPG in 2025, but his rush EPA jumped to 1.07 and he remains the clear HOU franchise QB with no roster threat. The two-year body of work shows a QB capable of top-8 output when the offense clicks, making him one of the higher-ceiling arms in this range. Floor is a mid QB2 given his passing volume; ceiling is a weekly starter. The playoff run (@PHI, @GB) is tough, so pair him with a matchup streamer.

sam darnold.verdict: 2024's 308-point ceiling is on file; SEA role is secure with strong CPOE
sam darnold.report: Darnold dipped from 308 points (18.1 PPG) in 2024 to 235 in 2025, but his 6.2 CPOE and 4.39 pass EPA/g still rank among the best here, and he's the locked-in SEA starter. The two seasons frame a wide but appealing outcome band — a fringe QB1 if the ceiling year repeats. Floor is dragged by negative rush EPA and a step down from his peak. Playoffs (@PHI, LAR, @CAR) are a mixed bag with one soft Week 17 spot.

bryce young.verdict: Trending up with real rushing volume (54 carries) — cheap late-round upside
bryce young.report: Young improved from 11.5 to 12.8 PPG and his 54 carries give him a rushing floor that separates him from pocket-only peers, even if his pass EPA stayed slightly negative. He's the clear CAR starter with only Kenny Pickett behind him, so the job is safe. Ceiling is a low-end QB1 if the arm efficiency catches up to the legs; floor is a streamable QB2. Playoff slate (CIN, @PIT, SEA) is middling.

fernando mendoza.verdict: Rookie with no NFL data and a genuine QB battle vs. Cousins/O'Connell
fernando mendoza.report: Mendoza carries zero pro production and the lowest projection (187) of any presumed starter here, with Kirk Cousins and Aidan O'Connell threatening the job on a rebuilding LV roster. Rookie QBs are volatile week-to-week and his hold on the role is far from certain. Ceiling is a late-season dynasty-relevant emergence; floor is a benching. Only worth a last-round dart or waiver stash.

geno smith.verdict: Sharp decline from 2024 peak; new NYJ situation and negative EPA are red flags
geno smith.report: Geno fell off a cliff, dropping from 266 points (15.6 PPG) in 2024 to just 174 (10.2 PPG) with a -4.86 pass EPA/g in 2025 — the trend line points down at age-mid-30s. A move to NYJ adds scheme and supporting-cast uncertainty. Ceiling banks on a rebound toward his 2024 form; floor is a matchup-only streamer who could lose snaps. Playoffs (@ARI, NE, MIN) offer a couple exploitable spots.

aaron rodgers.verdict: Steady but aging (21st year); modest pass EPA and no rushing floor
aaron rodgers.report: Rodgers dipped from 15.1 to 13.4 PPG with a barely-positive pass EPA (1.68) and negative rush EPA, and at 21 years of experience the decline and injury risk are real. He's the PIT starter but a crowded room (Rudolph, Allar, Howard) means any injury ends his season fast. Ceiling is a competent QB2; floor is a mid-season fade. The playoff draw (BAL, CAR, @TEN) has one great matchup in Week 16.

deshaun watson.verdict: Coming off lost season; projection of 124 says even Vegas doubts the role
deshaun watson.report: Watson has been a fantasy non-factor — 4.5 PPG in his last full season and no 2025 data — and the 124 projection reflects a likely part-time or contested role in CLE. Shedeur Sanders and others loom on the depth chart, and his history of injury and inconsistency caps any upside. Ceiling requires a full healthy starting job that's far from guaranteed; floor is irrelevance. Not draftable in standard formats.

jacoby brissett.verdict: 2025's 227 points looks fluky vs. -3.6 CPOE and a shaky ARI depth chart
jacoby brissett.report: Brissett posted a surprising 227 points (13.4 PPG) in 2025 but his -3.6 CPOE and -0.23 pass EPA suggest that output outran his efficiency and won't easily repeat. He faces Carson Beck and Gardner Minshew for the ARI job, making his snap count precarious. Ceiling is a repeat of the fluke season; floor is losing the job by midseason. Playoff matchups (NYJ, @NO, LV) are actually soft if he's still starting.

tua tagovailoa.verdict: New ATL team likely backing up Penix; injury history and 115 proj say avoid
tua tagovailoa.report: Tua's projection of 115 is the lowest here, reflecting that in ATL he sits behind Michael Penix on the depth chart despite the nominal QB1 label — a backup role in all likelihood. His scoring already slipped to 9.5 PPG with a long injury history dragging his availability. Ceiling only materializes via a Penix injury; floor is zero snaps. Undraftable outside deep two-QB leagues.

broncos d/st.verdict: Elite pass rush and secondary, top DST projection — worth a mid-round streaming anchor
broncos d/st.report: Denver posted 166 then 144 points the last two years, an elite unit driven by a fearsome pass rush and turnover-generating secondary. The 131 projection leads all DSTs and the sub-6.5 stdev signals a reliable weekly floor rather than boom-bust. Playoff slate is a mixed bag with @LV (great) and @NE (decent) but a tough BUF matchup in Week 16. This is the closest thing to a set-and-forget DST at ADP 90.

texans d/st.verdict: Most consistent unit in the pool — 10.2 ppg on a tiny 3.7 stdev is a rare floor
texans d/st.report: Houston jumped to 173 points (10.2 ppg) in 2025 with the lowest weekly stdev in the group at 3.7, meaning almost no dud weeks — the dream trait for a DST you actually start every week. The pass rush and ball-hawking secondary carry a high projection of 128. Playoff matchups (JAX home, @PHI, @GB) are neutral-to-favorable. Reliability plus a home JAX game in Week 15 make this a top-tier target.

steelers d/st.verdict: Falling from 135 to 113, but still a projectable veteran unit at a discount ADP
steelers d/st.report: Pittsburgh dipped from 135 to 113 points and the 7.2 stdev shows real week-to-week volatility, but the 126 projection expects a bounce-back with T.J. Watt anchoring the rush. The ceiling is a top-5 finish if the turnover luck normalizes. Playoff draw is rough with BAL and @TEN, though CAR in Week 16 is a plum spot. The ADP-118 price makes it decent value versus the top tier.

rams d/st.verdict: Steadily improving front seven, 101 to 125 arc points up for 2026
rams d/st.report: Los Angeles climbed from 101 to 125 points and the 123 projection expects continued growth from a young, disruptive pass rush. Moderate variance (5.4 stdev) keeps it usable weekly. Playoff schedule is workable with DAL at home Week 15 and division rematches at SEA and @TB. A solid mid-tier streamer with upside if the rush keeps ascending.

seahawks d/st.verdict: Explosive 185-point 2025 ceiling but the 8.2 stdev screams boom-or-bust
seahawks d/st.report: Seattle exploded to 185 points (10.9 ppg) in 2025, but the group-high 8.2 stdev means the production came in spiky bursts rather than steady scoring. The 121 projection sensibly regresses that outlier. Ceiling is the highest in the pool on any given week; floor is scary if the takeaways dry up. Playoff slate (@PHI, LAR, @CAR) is neutral. Best used as a matchup-based play rather than a weekly lock.

ravens d/st.verdict: Big projection bet on a bounce-back after a dismal 77-point 2025
ravens d/st.report: Baltimore cratered to just 77 points (4.5 ppg) in 2025 with high 7.4 variance, yet the 118 projection bets heavily on a talent-driven rebound. The name-brand pedigree and favorable division playoff draw (@PIT, CLE, @CIN) support the upside case. The floor case is real if last year's collapse wasn't a fluke. At ADP 134 the risk-reward is reasonable but this is a projection reach, not a proven unit.

lions d/st.verdict: Middling 91-point unit but a soft NFC North playoff schedule adds appeal
lions d/st.report: Detroit scored 91 then 100 points the last two years — consistently mediocre with league-average variance. The 108 projection assumes modest improvement from a scheme change and healthier front seven. The real draw is the playoff slate: @MIN, NYG, @CHI offers exploitable matchups against shaky offenses. A fine late-round streamer to target for Weeks 15-17.

eagles d/st.verdict: Talented front but declining output (138 to 126) caps the ceiling
eagles d/st.report: Philadelphia slid from 138 to 126 points and the 107 projection continues that downward drift despite an elite defensive line. Low 5.1 stdev keeps it steady if unspectacular. Playoff matchups are tough — SEA, HOU, and @SF are all capable offenses. A reasonable stream but the schedule and projection point to a mid-pack finish.

browns d/st.verdict: Huge 70-to-143 swing makes it a volatile upside dart at cheap ADP
browns d/st.report: Cleveland leapt from 70 points in 2024 to 143 in 2025, one of the biggest year-over-year swings, driven by an elite pass rush led by Myles Garrett. The 104 projection splits the difference, distrusting the spike. Ceiling is top-8 if the rush and takeaways hold; floor is ugly given the offense often puts the defense in bad spots. Playoff draw (@NYG, @BAL, IND) is mixed. Cheap enough at ADP 151 to gamble.

patriots d/st.verdict: Massive 48-to-133 improvement but sustainability is unproven
patriots d/st.report: New England surged from a dreadful 48 points in 2024 to 133 in 2025 as the rebuild took hold. The 100 projection is skeptical the leap fully sticks, though the low 5.1 stdev in 2025 was encouraging. Playoff schedule is brutal with @KC and @NYJ before a home DEN game. A speculative late pick — the trend is up but the sample is one year.

chiefs d/st.verdict: Steady low-end unit with a favorable Week 15 stream spot vs NE
chiefs d/st.report: Kansas City hovers around 90-98 points annually — a solid, unspectacular defense that benefits from game scripts with leads. The 100 projection fits that steady profile with modest variance. Playoff slate offers a juicy home NE game Week 15 but SF and @LAC are tougher. Fine as a matchup streamer, not a season-long starter.

chargers d/st.verdict: Consistent 117-119 unit, reliable mid-tier streaming option
chargers d/st.report: The Chargers scored 117 then 119 points in back-to-back years — remarkably stable production from an improving defense under a strong scheme. The 94 projection is a touch pessimistic given that consistency. Playoff matchups (SF, @MIA, KC) are neutral-to-tough. A dependable late-round grab with a decent weekly floor.

buccaneers d/st.verdict: Flat 89-91 point unit with high variance — deep-league streamer only
buccaneers d/st.report: Tampa Bay produced 91 then 89 points, a stagnant mid-pack profile, and the 6.9 stdev makes it unreliable week to week. The 93 projection expects more of the same. Playoff draw is favorable though — NO, @ATL, and home LAR offer exploitable spots in the division. Only worth rostering as a matchup play in the fantasy playoffs.

packers d/st.verdict: Collapsed from 140 to 77 points — projection remains cautious for good reason
packers d/st.report: Green Bay fell off a cliff, dropping from 140 points in 2024 to just 77 in 2025, and the 89 projection reflects that lost trust. There's rebound upside if the pass rush reasserts itself, but the recent trend is alarming. Playoff slate (MIA, @CHI, HOU) is workable. A speculative streamer that needs the defense to prove 2025 was the outlier.

colts d/st.verdict: Low-ceiling unit stuck in the 74-81 point range — waiver fodder
colts d/st.report: Indianapolis has scored 74 then 81 points, consistently near the bottom with little upside signal. The 88 projection is a mild bump but nothing suggests a leap. Playoff schedule (@TEN, CIN, @CLE) has a couple of soft spots against weak offenses. Draft only in deepest leagues or stream during the playoffs against TEN.

jaguars d/st.verdict: Wildly volatile 36-to-139 swing makes it a pure lottery ticket
jaguars d/st.report: Jacksonville is the most volatile unit here, scoring just 36 points in 2024 before exploding to 139 in 2025 — the projection of 81 splits the difference and distrusts the spike. The ceiling is real if the young defense's improvement holds, but the floor is disastrous. Playoff matchups (@HOU, @DAL, WSH) are a mixed bag. A high-risk late dart with genuine breakout equity.

bengals d/st.report: Cincinnati bottomed out at just 48 points (2.8 ppg) in 2025, one of the worst marks in the pool, and the 85 projection is optimistic even as a bounce-back. The defense has been a persistent weakness dragging down the roster. Playoff slate (@CAR, @IND, BAL) offers two soft spots worth a stream. Otherwise not draftable in standard formats.

bears d/st.verdict: Flat 94-95 point unit with heavy variance — matchup streamer at best
bears d/st.report: Chicago has scored 94-95 points in consecutive years but with alarming stdev (6.5-7.6), making it one of the more inconsistent options. The 84 projection expects more mediocrity. Playoff draw is tough opening at BUF before GB and DET at home. Deep-league or spot-start only.

49ers d/st.verdict: Declined to 62 points as injuries gutted the unit — tough playoff draw too
49ers d/st.report: San Francisco fell to just 62 points (3.6 ppg) in 2025 as injuries decimated the defense, and the 82 projection reflects a cautious rebound. There's name-brand upside if healthy, but the recent output is a warning. Playoff schedule is brutal with @LAC, @KC, and PHI — three high-powered offenses. Draft only if you believe in a full health-driven rebound.

jets d/st.verdict: Cratered to a league-worst 32 points — pure dart throw at the bottom
jets d/st.report: The Jets collapsed to just 32 points (1.9 ppg) in 2025, the worst mark in the entire pool, a stunning fall from 89 the year prior. The 81 projection banks on a rebound that the recent trend gives little reason to trust. Playoff matchups (@ARI, NE, MIN) include a couple of streamable spots. Last-resort waiver-wire option only.

saints d/st.verdict: Big 2025 jump (3.9→7.2 PPG) and playable playoff slate make it the better late-round stream
saints d/st.report: The Saints DST nearly doubled its output from 2024's dismal 3.9 PPG to a respectable 7.2 PPG in 2025, and the 2026 projection of 81 leads this pair. Weekly stdev of 6.0 is typical DST volatility — you're chasing splash plays, not consistency. The playoff run (@TB, ARI, @ATL) offers exploitable turnover-prone offenses in Weeks 16-17. This is a bench/waiver streamer, not a draftable asset — take it only in the very final rounds if you want a Week 1 fill.

panthers d/st.verdict: Lower 2025 output and projection, but tougher-to-read unit with soft Week 17 SEA matchup
panthers d/st.report: The Panthers posted 5.8 PPG in 2025 with a lower projection (75) than the Saints, and no 2024 baseline means less trend confidence. DST scoring here is TD/turnover dependent with a 5.4 weekly stdev, so streaming week-to-week is smarter than rostering season-long. The playoff schedule (CIN, @PIT, SEA) is mixed — Pittsburgh on the road in Week 16 is a concern, though the home slate has streamable spots. Purely a last-pick or waiver play; both units are essentially interchangeable stream candidates.

brandon aubrey.verdict: Elite leg with monster range in a high-scoring offense; the only K worth reaching for
brandon aubrey.report: Aubrey posted back-to-back elite seasons at 11.0 and 10.9 PPG with a rare rushing first down showing his unique leg strength on long attempts. His ceiling is the highest at the position thanks to Dallas's volume and his 60+ yard range, though weekly stdev (6.1) reflects some boom-bust nature. Floor is safe as the unquestioned starter with no competition. Playoff slate is mixed: @LAR is tough but JAX and NYG are exploitable indoor/dome-friendly setups.

cameron dicker.verdict: Consistent, low-variance leg in a good LAC offense; safe every-week starter
cameron dicker.report: Dicker delivered 10.4 then 9.8 PPG with the lowest variance in the top tier (stdev 4.5-4.9), making him a reliable set-and-forget option. His floor is among the safest at the position given accuracy and steady team scoring. Ceiling is capped compared to Aubrey without the massive-range upside. Playoff draw includes SF and KC which are competitive but the offense should keep him relevant.

jason myers.verdict: Big 2025 rebound to 11.5 PPG but 2024's 8.0 shows real volatility
jason myers.report: Myers exploded to 195 points and 11.5 PPG in 2025 after a mediocre 8.0 PPG in 2024, and that split is the caution flag — regression toward the middle is likely. As an 11-year veteran he's a secure starter with no competition. Ceiling is high if Seattle's offense sustains, floor is the 2024 version. Playoff schedule with @PHI is a real negative, though LAR and @CAR are workable.

ka'imi fairbairn.verdict: Steady Houston volume with strong 2025 output; missed a couple games
ka'imi fairbairn.report: Fairbairn improved from 9.8 to 11.2 PPG and carries a high 6.5 stdev signaling boom weeks in a Houston offense that should generate chances. He missed a couple games in 2025 (15 advanced-usage games) which is a minor injury flag for a 10-year vet. Ceiling is top-five at the position; floor is solid as the entrenched starter. Playoffs feature two tough road spots (@PHI, @GB) that dent his December appeal.

harrison mevis.verdict: Strong-legged young kicker inheriting the high-powered Rams job; limited sample
harrison mevis.report: Mevis showed 9.0 PPG across just 9 games, so the sample is thin, but he steps into a Rams offense that produces plenty of scoring opportunities. His projection of 160 reflects optimism about full-season volume. Ceiling is a top-six finish in a good offense; floor is uncertainty from the small track record and youth. Playoff slate (DAL, @SEA, @TB) is neutral to slightly favorable.

cam little.verdict: Ascending young leg with elite range; trending up from 7.3 to 9.5 PPG
cam little.report: Little jumped from 7.3 to 9.5 PPG in his second season and has demonstrated exceptional long-range ability, giving him real breakout upside. Jacksonville's offense is improving which supports his volume outlook. Floor is reasonable given a secure job and no competition; ceiling could crack the top five if the Jags score more. Playoff road games @HOU and @DAL are tougher, but WSH in Week 17 is favorable.

eddy pineiro.verdict: Big 2025 jump but SF offense variance and missed games cloud outlook
eddy pineiro.report: Pineiro nearly doubled his 2024 output (6.1 to 8.7 PPG) but the 5.8 stdev and two missed games (14 advanced-usage) inject risk. San Francisco's offense provides scoring chances but leans toward TDs over field goals when healthy. Ceiling is a mid-range K1; floor is the injury-and-inconsistency scenario. Playoff schedule is brutal with @LAC, @KC, and PHI all being difficult matchups.

jake bates.verdict: Detroit's high-octane offense gives a stable, low-variance floor
jake bates.report: Bates put up 9.3 then 8.5 PPG with excellent consistency (stdev 3.3-3.6) inside one of the league's best offenses, which caps FG volume slightly but boosts XP totals. His floor is among the safest at the position. Ceiling is limited because Detroit scores TDs rather than settling for field goals. Playoff draw (@MIN, NYG, @CHI) is mostly favorable indoor and weak-defense spots.

harrison butker.verdict: KC offense rebound in 2025; low variance but modest ceiling
harrison butker.report: Butker recovered from a rough 5.6 PPG in 2024 to 8.5 in 2025 with tight variance (3.8 stdev), reflecting KC's return to form. As a longtime reliable starter he offers a safe floor. Ceiling is capped by Kansas City's red-zone efficiency limiting FG chances. Playoff schedule (NE, SF, @LAC) is neutral with some risk in the SF and LAC matchups.

chris boswell.verdict: Elite 2024 crashed to 8.6 in 2025; PIT offense limits the rebound case
chris boswell.report: Boswell's 11.1 PPG in 2024 collapsed to 8.6 in 2025, a stark decline that raises real concern for a 12-year veteran. His draft rank fell to 237 reflecting the market's skepticism. Ceiling is a bounce-back if Pittsburgh's offense improves; floor is continued mediocrity. Playoff slate (BAL, CAR, @TEN) offers two soft spots that could aid a late run.

chase mclaughlin.verdict: Steady Tampa leg, mild decline, dependable mid-range option
chase mclaughlin.report: McLaughlin logged 9.5 then 8.9 PPG in a competent Tampa offense, providing reliable if unspectacular production. His job is secure with no competition listed. Ceiling is a low-end K1 finish; floor is safe given the offense's scoring capacity. Playoffs (NO, @ATL, LAR) skew favorable with dome and weak-defense matchups.

will reichard.verdict: Young kicker trending up in a Minnesota offense with upside
will reichard.report: Reichard improved from 7.4 to 9.3 PPG in his second year with reduced variance, a positive trajectory. Minnesota's offense should provide steady scoring chances. Ceiling is a mid K1 if the Vikings offense clicks; floor is reasonable as the secure starter. Playoff schedule (DET, WSH, @NYJ) is mostly favorable outside the DET matchup.

tyler loop.verdict: Solid rookie season in Baltimore's strong offense; sophomore upside
tyler loop.report: Loop delivered 8.2 PPG as a rookie in a high-scoring Baltimore offense, a respectable debut with room to grow. His job appears secure as the starter. Ceiling is a K1 finish given the Ravens' scoring, floor is typical for a young kicker with one year of tape. Playoff draw (@PIT, CLE, @CIN) is a mix of division games with variable weather risk.

cairo santos.verdict: Veteran in an improving Chicago offense; modest but rising output
cairo santos.report: Santos ticked up from 6.2 to 7.5 PPG as Chicago's offense showed signs of life, and the 5.1 stdev hints at occasional boom weeks. As a 12-year vet he's a secure but unexciting option. Ceiling depends on the Bears offense taking a real step forward; floor is low-end streamer territory. Playoff schedule (@BUF, GB, DET) is one of the tougher slates.

evan mcpherson.verdict: High-variance leg with elite offense upside if Cincy stays healthy
evan mcpherson.report: McPherson jumped from a dismal 5.2 to 7.9 PPG with high variance (5.9 stdev), and his ceiling is tied to Cincinnati's explosive-but-inconsistent offense. His draft rank of 256 shows the market wants proof of stability. Ceiling is a top-eight finish if the Bengals score at full capacity; floor is the volatility scenario. Playoffs (@CAR, @IND, BAL) offer two favorable spots.

nick folk.verdict: Ancient but reliable; low ceiling in a middling Atlanta offense
nick folk.report: Folk, in his 19th season, produced 6.3 then 7.4 PPG with low variance in 2025, showing steady if unremarkable output. Age is an ever-present risk but he remains accurate. Ceiling is a back-end K1; floor is streamer level in a modest offense. Playoff schedule (@WSH, TB, NO) is fairly favorable with dome and weak-defense games.

trey smack.verdict: Unproven rookie in Green Bay with a backup pushing for the job
trey smack.report: Smack has zero NFL production and faces Lucas Havrisik listed as the #2, making his starting role less certain than others in this group. The Green Bay offense would provide good volume if he wins and holds the job. Ceiling is a mid K1 in a strong offense; floor is a possible in-season benching or platoon. Playoff slate (MIA, @CHI, HOU) is neutral.

jake elliott.verdict: Declining output despite elite offense; TDs cap his FG volume
jake elliott.report: Elliott slipped from 7.8 to a disappointing 6.4 PPG in 2025 as Philadelphia's TD-heavy offense limited field-goal chances. Despite the strong team context his fantasy value has eroded, reflected in a 288 draft rank. Ceiling is limited even with the offense's scoring; floor is streamer territory. Playoff schedule (SEA, HOU, @SF) is neutral to tough.
